#1285. De Bruyne future at Napoli uncertain as possibility of January exit emerges

Kevin De Bruyne is facing an uncertain future at club level, and local reports suggest that the Belgian superstar could potentially even leave as early as January.

De Bruyne has been with Napoli for almost 18 months, having joined on a free transfer at the end of his Manchester City contract in the summer of 2025.

The 35-year-old has started in all 11 of Napoli’s Serie A matches so far this season. This has followed a disappointing 2024-25 season on an individual level, which saw De Bruyne miss over four months of action with a major hamstring injury midway through the campaign.

De Bruyne also found himself wrapped up in controversy at the end of last season, when he said that he was ‘happy’ to see head coach Antonio Conte leave, suggesting that he and the coach had a ‘very different vision of football’, adding “I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position.”

Conte has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri, who has endured a wretched start to his Napoli career. The Partenopei have lost seven of their first 15 matches under Allegri’s stewardship, they are in 10th place in the Serie A table, already 14 points off the league leaders after 11 matches.

They have also lost three of their first four Champions League matches and are currently in 27th place in the European standings, at risk of missing out on qualification to the play-off round. Direct qualification for the round of 16 is already looking impossible.

In spite of his obvious quality and experience, De Bruyne’s first year-and-a-half in Italy have not worked out as well as he would have hoped, and now, there have been suggestions that he could leave as early as January.

Napoli, who had a relatively quiet summer transfer window, are expected to make several moves in January, both in terms of incomings and outgoings: Monday’s reports indicate that Allegri wants at least three or four new additions, and reports over the weekend claimed that Lorenzo Lucca, Noa Lang and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa are among the most likely names to be sacrificed.

Monday’s reports from Il Mattino add that De Bruyne’s future is also uncertain, despite the fact that Allegri has ‘done everything’ to get the Belgian onside. Il Mattino adds that it ‘drastic decisions’ regarding De Bruyne’s future during the January transfer window can not be ruled out at this stage.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

This guy is getting too big for his britches, especially since he is now a shell of his best which was never world class anyway.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

#1283. He Played With Man Utd Icon David Beckham - Now He’s 20x Richer Than Both

David Beckham is among the richest individuals in football but his wealth pales in comparison to a former Premier League star's staggering net worth.

The former Manchester United midfielder has become an entrepreneur since hanging up his boots in 2013 and took on his main business venture a year later. He exercised an option to take a Major League Soccer club to Miami and in 2018 his wish was granted as Inter Miami were launched as MLS' 25th club.

Beckham is one of many legendary footballers who have turned to entrepreneurship post-retirement and many of them have been far more successful as a business person. That's the case for one of his former teammates whose net worth has reached an unimaginable level.

Beckham saw out his career in the USA with LA Galaxy before becoming a co-owner of Inter Miami, but he spent most of his playing days in Europe. His time in Italy came with AC Milan, where he played with big names, including Brazilian icon Ronaldinho.

Former Arsenal midfielder Mathieu Flamini linked up with Beckham in Milan, spending five years with the Rossoneri before returning to the Emirates in 2016. The Frenchman didn't quite reach the heights of England's former captain but he has more than outperformed the former England captain with his business venture.

Back in 2025, The Sunday Times Rich List reported that Beckham and his wife Victoria had a combined net worth of £500 million. That wealth came from not only the Miami expansion but other ventures.

Flamini only needed one to accumulate a remarkable net worth of £10 billion and that came through GFBiochemicals, a biochemical company he founded in 2008. Specialising in producing levulinic acid, this reduces CO2 emissions in manufacturing processes for items such as detergents by as much as 80 percent.

The former France midfielder is GF Biochemicals' chief executive and co-founder, which also helps create substitutes for fossil-based materials and is a leader in environmental sustainability. His astonishing riches have come after a relatively well-paid career in football where, during his time at Arsenal, he won three FA Cups and played in the 2006 Champions League final.

Flamini's post-playing career success hasn't been born out of luck or connections, as he has always held a special connection with the environment. He explained this during an interview with Harvard Business Review in June of this year:

"Football was a childhood dream but the environment has always played an important role in my life. Having grown up in the South of France, I’ve always felt close to nature and the sea. When I was a child, I remember watching documentaries with my family and picking up plastic waste on the beaches."

Flamini added: "I developed an environmental awareness at a very early age. Even during my football career, I wondered how we could find solutions to global warming, and considered the impact humans can have on the environment, but also on their own health."

It was during his time at the San Siro when the Frenchman first saw a path towards becoming a businessman: "When I joined AC Milan at 24, I was one of the youngest players on the squad. Many of my team-mates were already involved in other ventures, which led me to start thinking about entrepreneurship at a very early stage."

He added: "Then there were encounters and opportunities that steered me towards the chemical sector. We developed partnerships with universities in Italy, we met scientists and engineers, and a research group was set up."

Flamini saw a gap in the market which he delved into: "At some point, we decided to focus on a molecule identified by the US Department of Energy as one of the 12 molecules of the future. It showed great potential to replace many petroleum-derived molecules and thus accelerate the transition to a more sustainable chemical industry. However, this platform molecule, levulinic acid, had not yet been developed on an industrial scale. There was therefore a real opportunity here."

Some people's businesses have helped them earn billions after retiring.

The 42-year-old is the second-richest footballer of all time, sitting behind Brunei royal family member Faiq Bolkiah, but he ranks above Beckham, Cristiano Ronaldo and David Beckham. It's an astonishing story and makes him one of the richest self-made former athletes in history.

#1282. Forest Green apologise for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home match due to 'mistake'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 07:03 EST, 9 November 2026

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home game, labelling it as 'human error' and a 'mistake' from the club.

Remembrance Day is November 11 with Forest Green's sole fixture around that date having been Saturday's 2-0 FA Cup first-round defeat at Luton Town. Both teams commemorated the occasion ahead of kick-off at Kenilworth Road.

Forest Green's last home fixture prior to that was a 2-2 draw with Harrogate Town on October 31 in the National League.

That encounter at The New Lawn saw supporters of the fifth-tier side take to a fan forum post-match questioning why nothing was in place for Remembrance Day - due to their then-forthcoming clash with Luton being an away tie.

Forest Green CEO Dane Vince replied on the club's Fan Advisory Board, admitting it was an oversight on their part.

'The lack of Remembrance at a home game is simply down to a human error/mistake on the club,' he wrote.

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for not commemorating Remembrance Day at a home game (National League side pictured doing so during Saturday's FA Cup 2-0 defeat at Luton)

Forest Green failed to do so in their home draw vs Harrogate on October 31, calling it a 'mistake'

Vince continued that a condensed schedule in this period didn't help matters, but still acknowledged that the club should have done more.

'It didn't help that we had a sizable number of games in a small time frame (including the FA Cup replay) beforehand; albeit that isn't an excuse, we should have got this right.'

Following the incident, Vince confirmed that Forest Green would contact the Royal British Legion for advice on future commemorations to ensure this wouldn't happen again. He also underlined that the missed home commemoration did not signal any change in the club's support for Remembrance or the Royal British Legion.

'This was a simple error/mistake,' he reiterated.

#1281. Cisse: ‘Italy is full of strong young players, I want to prove I should be here’

Alphadjo Cisse has spoken about the moment he found out he had been called up to the Italy national team for the first time, says that he wants to prove what he has to offer during his first camp with the Nazionale and says that there is plenty of young talent in Serie A and Serie B: ‘Let me tell you’.

Cisse was included in the Italy national team squad for the first time last week, ahead of Nations League fixtures against France on Thursday and Belgium on Sunday.

It has been a remarkable rise to the top for the 20-year-old, who was playing in Serie B with Catanzaro last season. He is now Milan’s leading goalscorer across all competitions in 2026-27 and has already bettered his goalscoring tally from last season with eight from 15 appearances so far.

The versatile attacker spoke in-depth about his career to date and his first Italy call-up in a recent interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio.

The latest Italy squad was announced on Thursday evening, just before Cisse and Milan kicked off against Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Cisse found out that he had been selected for the Azzurri while in the media zone in San Siro.

“I was on my way to do the pre-match interviews ahead of Ferencvaros in the Europa League and they stopped me and said: ‘Alpha, they’ve called you up to the national team … the senior national team!’. I had the game to play, so it only sunk in later,” he recalled (via TMW).

“I want to prove that I should be there. They’d been talking to me about it for about 10 days, but it was still up in the air. This is my big chance. I haven’t had the chance to stop and reflect on my journey here, but football moves quickly!”

Cisse is a glaring example of what can happen when young players are given opportunities at the top level. He feels that there are plenty more uncovered gems knocking about in Serie A and Serie B.

“Italy is full of strong, young players, let me tell you. It just depends on the opportunities you’re given. A lot have come through over the last few months, myself included, and I’m sure that there will be lots more in the near future.

“Once you get to a certain level, it becomes amazing. I was impressed by Pisilli more than anyone: He’s so strong. I knew about him before, but playing with him made me understand his strength.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Well said Cisse. There is bundles of talent and if they are used along with new infrastructure then Italy will get to the top again.

Back in September, Celtic went into the break on the back of three straight defeats, and Martin O'Neill was left contemplating his own future. The Bhoys now have a moment's rest from the criticism, but some players will be worried about their position in this squad.

Here we take a look at the players who are at risk of being cut by O'Neill in the January transfer window.

McCowan has had a tough season so far, and it all started with his disastrous cameo against LASK in that infamous Champions League collapse. The midfielder was slaughtered by fans after that game, and some of it crossed the line into abuse.

McCowan has come back into the fray a little of late, making two substitute appearances in the last two league games, but it doesn't feel as though O'Neill fully trusts him, and this is not a young player.

McCowan is 28 years of age and he cannot get into a team that has a particularly poor midfield and a clear lack of depth in the middle. That is an indictment in itself, and we have already seen reports that McCowan could be offloaded if Celtic can find a replacement.

Tounekti has had a tough time of things this season. He has been heavily criticised for his lack of consistency, and for his predictability as a winger. He is somewhere between unable and unwilling to repeatedly run at and beat his men, regularly turning inside or taking the easy option.

The Tunisia international has talent, there is little doubt, but he has been given repeated opportunities this season amid injury issues on the left, and he has repeatedly fallen short of expectations. In fact, in 17 appearances across all competitions, Tounekti has one assist and no goals. That's just not good enough for a winger who plays for a team that generally dominate opponents domestically. Being a winger for Celtic, especially under O'Neill's direct style. should be a dream.

Fans have run out of patience when it comes to Tounekti, and it feels as though O'Neill's patience is also wearing thin. To make matters worse for the winger, Jota and Yang Hyun-jun are now nearing full fitness, while Callum Osmand has also impressed on the left.

O'Neill may feel as though he has enough on that side, and if the right-footed Tounekti isn't going to compete on the other side, a loan move, in particular, could be seen as a good option.

#1278. Aston Villa Must Axe 'Awful' Boubacar Kamara After Man Utd Shocker

Aston Villa will be absolutely furious with themselves after blowing a two-goal lead twice at Old Trafford to be held to a 4-4 draw by Manchester United on Sunday evening.

The visitors were 2-0 up inside four minutes after goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson, before Bruno Fernandes and ex-Villan Youri Tielemans got the hosts level before half-time. But John McGinn and Leon Goretzka scored inside the opening eight minutes of the half to restore the two-goal cushion.

However, injury-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw United nick a late draw, leaving Villa 10th in the Premier League table heading into the international break, with just three wins from their ten games so far.

But while the manager would usually be the one to receive criticism for such results, the blame is being passed on to the players by most fans, who acknowledge that Unai Emery has been dealt a rough hand this season after the entire spine of his squad stripped away during the summer.

Replacements were brought in, but the majority of Villa's summer signings are struggling to make an immediate impact. However, while speaking after the game on his social media account, club legend Gabriel Agbonlahor called out a senior player who has been around for several seasons as someone who has been 'awful' this season.

"Kamara can't move and has been awful this season!" he wrote.

He then continued and vented his anger at several other players.

"Maatsen can't defend against anyone. Defensively we lack pace. Goalkeeper [has] been found out with crosses. Barkley comes on and plays like he's on the 5-a-side pitch.. Zero game management is why the manager stormed off. Crap."

Since Kamara joined the club on a free transfer, it's fair to say that he has established himself as one of the best and most underrated midfielders in the Premier League under Emery.

But the Frenchman has been way off his usual standards this season, and it's clear that right now his reputation from previous campaigns is saving him from being dropped from the team.

Emery has always been a very loyal coach, and he likes to let people try and play through their bad form. But performances like the one against Man Utd are costing Villa from picking up vital points, and they need to be stamped out. A bit of time on the sideline to get himself back to his usual level could be ideal, and would also give other players a chance to step up.

Lamar Bogarde has found himself out of the matchday squad at times this season, but he performed well last year as a utility man. Alongside him, Goretzka, John McGinn, and Joao Gomes are all capable of stepping into that role to give him a rest.

With a big game against Sunderland next up after the international break, followed by a trip to Istanbul to take on Galatasaray, Villa must get victories, and that may mean leaving Kamara out until he finds his level again.

Published: 13:14 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:15 EST, 9 November 2026

Wayne Rooney has led the praise for football super-agent Paul Stretford as the industry heavyweight was honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards.

Stretford, alongside Kenneth Shepherd, received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's Awards in recognition of their longstanding careers and work on Soccer Aid for Unicef.

He has worked by Rooney's side for more than 20 years, and has recently appeared on the former footballer's reality TV show, which he fronts alongside wife Coleen.

Rooney presented Stretford with the award himself, alongside Toni Duggan and comedian Paddy McGuinness. Theo Walcott and Jamie Carragher hosted the ceremony.

Rooney said of his agent and close friend: 'Paul in particular has had a major influence on my life since I was a teenager and has guided my career.

'Both Paul and Kenneth are very deserving of this award. It is not before time and I'm delighted for both of them. The work they've done on Soccer Aid is phenomenal too.'

Wayne Rooney (centre) has lauded close friend and football super agent Paul Stretford (right)

Stretford doesn't just look after Rooney, having also worked with the likes of Harry Maguire since founding Proactive Sports Management, now known as Triple S Sports Group, in 1987.

Shepherd, meanwhile, has been instrumental in the success of the Soccer Aid initiative which has raised more than £137million for Unicef since it launched in 2006.

McGuinness added: 'I'm so proud to pay tribute to a duo who have had a profound impact on football and two figures we've both had the pleasure of working with over the years. Together, they built the Triple S Group into a dynamic force in British and international football.'

England assistant manager Anthony Barry also carried out an exclusive Q&A at the event, which saw Tyler Alexander-Arnold, brother of England defender Trent, also scoop a top award.

The brother of the Real Madrid star represents Jordan Henderson, Jarrod Bowen and Andy Robertson as well as his sibling, who saw his PLG Agency bought by Gersh talent agency in May of this year.

#1276. Roma will not release Molina for Argentina duty despite World Cup ban being reduced

Monday’s reports confirm that Roma will not release Nahuel Molina for international duty with Argentina this week, despite his seven-game ban for his antics at the end of the World Cup final being reduced to just four games.

Molina had originally been handed a seven-match ban and a $77,000 fine by FIFA for violent conduct at the end of the 2026 World Cup final, which saw Spain defeat Argentina 1-0 in extra-time. His teammate and former Roma midfielder Leandro Paredes was banned for 10 matches and fined $90,000.

On Saturday, it was confirmed that Molina’s ban had been reduced from seven matches to four, and given that he served the first three games of his suspension during the September-October international break, he now has just one game of his ban left.

Argentina will be involved in two international friendlies during the November international break, against Uruguay and then Costa Rica, and Molina is now eligible to play in the second one of those games.

According to reports Il Messaggero, Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni had attempted to hand Molina a last-minute call-up to the national team squad for the friendlies coming up in November. The latest Argentina squad was announced a few days before Molina’s ban was formally reduced.

However, Roma have reportedly informed the Argentine FA that they will not be releasing Molina for international duty in November, and he is instead expected to report for training with the Giallorossi on Wednesday.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1275. Because of Farke: Wilfried Gnonto Has Played His Final Game For Leeds

Leeds United look to have a good chance of finishing in the top half of the Premier League table this season after their opening 10 matches.

Leeds started the campaign positively, but there would have been a worry that they would slip towards the bottom three following a run of five top flight games without a win.

While it wasn't pretty and the best game they will play this term, the Yorkshire outfit did pick up their first three points since thrashing Newcastle United at Elland Road in September, as they beat Tottenham Hotspur thanks to Noah Okafor's late goal.

Leeds have the third-best defensive record in the Premier League, having conceded just eight times, but there will be concerns about an attack that has scored 10 times in the same number of fixtures.

Still, Farke would have been happy to see Okafor net his second of the season against Spurs, joining Jayden Bogle on that number, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who is attracting Man Utd interest amid talk of a new Leeds contract, ahead on three.

It would be no surprise to see the Yorkshire club dip into the transfer market in January to add to their attacking options, with the club already being linked with a number of players.

According to reports, Leeds hold an interest in Galatasaray playmaker Gabriel Sara, who has impressed in English football previously with Norwich City.

Jack Rudoni of Coventry City is another player catching the attention of scouts, while they have been interested in Lyon's Pavel Sulc for months, although any move for him is on the back-burner after he suffered an injury that is set to keep him on the sidelines until March.

The Whites have also been linked with a move for Harvey Elliott, whose career continues to stall as he struggles to find the right home away from Liverpool.

Should a new attacking signing arrive in January, or next summer, it would only further cement the fact that Wilfried Gnonto has no future at Elland Road.

Despite being something of a key attacking player for Leeds during their time in the Championship, Gnonto was able to replicate that sort of form in the Premier League.

It quickly became clear last season that Farke didn't fancy the Italy international as he looked to ensure the club stayed in the Premier League the year after they won promotion from the Championship.

In the summer, Gnonto ended up joining Serie A outfit Fiorentina on loan, in a deal which the BBC reported gave La Viola the option to buy the 23-year-old permanently for £18m, including the loan fee and future add-ons.

The winger has started life with the Italian club by scoring one goal in 10 appearances, and you would think he needs to significantly improve that number if there is any chance of a permanent deal happening.

Still, one change Farke has made in recent weeks means that Gnonto has no future at the club even if he does return to Yorkshire at the end of the season.

Much of the club's success this season has come from the German coach using a 3-5-2 formation, and it looks as though it's here to stay after delivering another three points against Tottenham.

Gnonto was already struggling to get into a team that used 4-3-3 and 3-4-3 systems last term, and he would need to play either as a wing-back, behind the strikers, or as a striker in Farke's trusted new set-up.

That simply isn't going to happen, and it would now be a big surprise if the Italian attacker ever wears a Leeds shirt again.

He has been outstanding for Leeds United under Daniel Farke this season

#1273. West Ham Flop is Now Outscoring Ballon d’Or Winner Harry Kane

It can be hard for anyone to lead the line and be expected to become the main goalscorer for a team, especially in the Premier League.

For teams like West Ham United, it feels like they've spent longer than most waiting for a truly threatening and, crucially, consistent centre-forward. They've tried plenty, but few have clicked for prolonged periods.

Of course, at present, they can turn to the likes of Jarrod Bowen as a reliable and prolific creator coming in off the right, and elsewhere in recent times, they found joy turning Michail Antonio into their star striker for a decent spell.

While West Ham have had plenty of talismanic talents over the past two decades, many still believe that their lack of a reliable go-to man up top for so long is part of the reason behind their steady slump towards relegation last term.

One of the players fans hoped could have turned their offensive fortunes around was former Borussia Dortmund forward Niclas Fullkrug, whose time with the Hammers was heavily hampered by injuries, struggling to perform in an admittedly struggling side, loan spells and more; but now, the towering target man looks to have got his career back on track.

While Harry Kane was lifting the Ballon d'Or, his former teammate was being investigated by London authorities.

The German international, who also played an impressive role at the most recent Euros back in 2024, is now out front in the race for the 'Torjagerkanone' award - Bundesliga's golden boot award.

Fullkrug, 33, is currently beating out the likes of Patrick Schick, Michael Olise, and even this year's Ballon d’Or winner, Harry Kane.

The classic number nine has hit nine goals in nine games, with one of the best shot conversion rates in the league. For context, he only managed five goal contributions in the Premier League during his two years at the London club.

Now plying his trade at the sharp end of a resurgent Werder Bremen side, Fullkrug seems to be enjoying an equally promising upturn at his boyhood club, having returned there after 12 years this season.

His height, strength and power have all come in handy in helping 'The River Islanders' climb to sixth in the table, but the main man has also found himself the central character in plenty of headlines besides his output on the pitch.

In the wake of a narrow and tense defeat to Stuttgart this past weekend, the Hanover-born bagsman took issue with one reporter fielding questions about his inclusion in Jurgen Klopp's latest Germany selection ahead of the upcoming international break.

Speaking with ZDF’s 'Aktuelles Sportstudio', Fullkrug was quick to pull up the reporter, simply responding: "A little respect. We just lost a game. That's not in my head right now."

Found an error? Send it info@www.givemesport.com so it can be corrected.

Nevertheless, a lot of eyes are understandably back on the big centre-forward, and it'll be interesting to see just how much of a part he could be set to play back in the shirt for his country. The ex-Liverpool manager can't ignore the stats, but how much he truly fancies him in competitive squads moving forward is up for debate.

Whether or not he keeps up his impressive record this campaign also remains to be seen, too; you can be sure England captain Kane will have plenty to say about that over the coming weeks and months. Still, to have gone from another experiment, quickly bought and sold by Sullivan, Gold, Kretínsky and co., it just goes to show that while not everyone makes it in the Premier League, it doesn't mean they aren't capable of doing it on the big stage.

#1272. A failed spell at Wolves almost saw him walk away from football ...now Danny Armstrong is idolised in Romania as he attempts to lead Dinamo Bucharest back to former glories

Published: 13:42 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:52 EST, 9 November 2026

The daughter says: ‘Da’. Darby Armstrong, all of two years old, is not calling out for her father, Danny.

‘She is saying “Yes” in Romanian. She can count to ten in Romanian,’ says her proud father. She may have to learn to count higher, and quickly, to chart her father’s figures in the Superliga with Dinamo Bucharest.

Armstrong sits in an upmarket restaurant in the beautiful suburbs of Bucharest with a park stretching towards a lake. He sips ginger tea with honey and engages with waiters, diners and children who approach him for a chat and a photograph.

‘Darby is a bit bemused by it,’ he says. ‘We were in the mall there and a guy wanted a pic. I could see her looking up to see what all the fuss was about.’

Armstrong could be forgiven for being ever so slightly bemused himself. At 29, he has taken a few dunts and not just from enthusiastic full-backs. Success has hardly been overnight.

‘I nearly gave up once,’ he says quietly. ‘Another time I thought it was all over and I was looking at one-to-one coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Danny Armstrong is hailed after his match-winning heroics in a crucial win over UTA Arad

He survived, though. He is a hero at Dinamo. There is a clamour on matchday when he comes out of the tunnel. The ultras, high behind a goal, chant his name with a fervour that suddenly breaks out in red flares and manic jumping.

It is a long way from Ayr. Armstrong knows he did not walk it alone. His saviours include John McGlynn, who brought him to Raith Rovers, George Cairns, who convinced him to stay at Hamilton, and Scott Sellars, the youth coach who advised him to leave Wolverhampton Wanderers for first team football.

He also took inspiration from many team-mates, including Kieran Tierney who was once his room-mate in a Scotland under-age team,

‘I was meant to be rooming with another left-back but he pulled out and this young player from Celtic came in,’ recalls Armstrong. ‘He wasn’t even in the squad initially and now he is Scotland’s best left-back alongside Robbo.

‘I used to play against KT so many times and I have great respect for him, playing so many games for Celtic, getting that move to Arsenal and coming back to Scotland to win trophies. The setbacks he has had… he’s an inspiration.

‘He has resilience. He has motivation. He took the half opportunity that was offered to him and ran with it.’

Armstrong has done the same in Bucharest. He has been bolstered by his past. ‘It builds you,’ he says of his experience. ‘There have been tough spells but you can look back and make sense of them and see how they have helped you. Football takes a lot of work.’

Armstrong has thrived in Romania since making the leftfield switch to Dinamo Bucharest

It takes a lot of belief too. That can be a capricious quality, seemingly dependent on the winds of fortune.

Armstrong can point to two hat-tricks that gave him faith in a time of need. ‘I scored a hat-trick for Hamilton in a youth game at Auchenhowie against Rangers,’ he says. ‘That came after I had been convinced to stick at it.’

He also scored three last season in the derby against Steaua. ‘That was crazy,’ he says. ‘I don’t think I have realised even yet how big it was. People tell me it was the greatest day in their lives. We hadn’t beaten them in five or six years. We were also in a bad spot with poor form. And then I score three. It gives me goosebumps even now.’

He adds: ‘There is a real football culture here. It means so much to people and I love that. It actually wasn’t too hard to come here because I had looked at it a year earlier but stayed on at Kilmarnock. When Dinamo came in and showed me videos and talked about the history, I was on board.’

There was one decisive factor. ‘I knew it was time to try to make a name for myself somewhere else. I wanted to test myself, keep myself open to other opportunities, try to get to the highest level I can get.’

He is professionally coy about the prospect of international football, having again missed out on Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest Scotland squad. He maintains the line of concentrating on his club form, having a dream to play for his country, and hoping to be noticed.

Armstrong was a big hit at Kilmarnock and has long been mooted for a Scotland call-up

His performances in Romania, though, have been so outstanding that there may be the odd glance from the Pocognoli camp at just what is happening at Dinamo. They may have to be quick as Armstrong qualifies for Ireland too.

He plays in a wide right role, with the freedom to cut inside and become a playmaker. His manager, Nuno Campos, has faith in him. He is the latest in a line of characters who have led him from doubt to conviction.

There is no hesitation. ‘It was McGlynn who saved me,’ says Armstrong. But there were previous tribulations that required the intervention of football folk and Armstrong is immensely grateful.

‘I had been going up to Hamilton from Ayr every night as a kid, playing at the weekend, and by the time I was about 15 I think I was drained. I felt I was missing out on other things in life. It was tough on my parents, too, who did everything for me. The family always sacrificed themselves for me.’

His parents told George Cairns, Hamilton coach, that their son did not want to continue. The reply was instant: ‘Get him up here and I will have a chat with him.’

The crisis passed after this talk and that hat-trick against Rangers. But further tribulations were to come.

Armstrong's relentless drive and enthusiasm have made him a standout player in Romania

Armstrong headed to Wolverhampton Wanderers, spurning an offer by Rangers under Mark Warburton and Davie Weir. ‘That was a mistake,’ he says. He was never near first team football at Wolves though the club wanted to retain him. After a chat with Scott Sellars, he took the chance to leave and start again.

‘That was very, very difficult,’ he says. ‘I did not play from May to November. I was sitting by the phone, urging it to ring with an offer. I had thoughts about packing it all in and going into coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Then an unlikely Superman came to the rescue in the shape of McGlynn, then Raith manager. ‘That changed everything, everything,’ says Armstrong.

A bounce game was organised to assess the player but Armstrong admits the team’s performance was awful. ‘I was very much part of that,’ he says.

He did much better in another friendly but budget considerations meant McGlynn could offer only a nine-game contract. ‘It was a couple of hundred quid a week but it meant everything to me.’ Five goals in nine games led to an extended contract.

‘He is a genius,’ says Armstrong. ‘He is so big on detail, detail, detail. He is a fantastic football coach. It’s an obsession for him.

‘I have never met a man like him. He saved my football career and made me believe I could make it.’

John McGlynn helped save Armstrong's career by taking him under his wing at Raith Rovers

After a spell at Ross County, Armstrong flourished under Derek McInnes at Kilmarnock and the move to Romania offered further scope for growth.

‘It was a bit difficult at first settling in but now my partner, Lauren, and Darby love it. We have made friends,’ he says.

At this a couple of waiters approach the table with grins and cheery banter. Armstrong responds with a warm handshake and that half-embrace that signals another acquiescence to yet another picture.

‘The big difference this season is the coach,’ says Armstrong. ‘He has come in and completely changed the environment and the atmosphere. He has brought fun back and he makes you want to come into training.’

Dinamo are now sitting joint-top of the league. ‘The first goal has to be European football, getting this club back to where it belongs,’ he says.

Armstrong has his sights set on an historic Romanian title and is not ruling out a longer stay

The Dinamo fans, who have not witnessed a league title in 20 years, sense Superliga glory. ‘We are a good side and we play nice stuff,’ says Armstrong. ‘But let’s take it game by game.’

He has the same laid-back attitude to his contract. ‘It expires at the end of the season and there is an option there but we leave all that to after Christmas.’

He is happy in Bucharest but knows the fate of a footballer is never predictable. ‘It is a wonderful place. The fans are great and the manager has faith in me.’

He points out that Campos wants him to be a ‘monster’. This is an instruction to be powerful and innovative in the final third.

The next night Armstrong swivels just outside the box and hits a wonderful shot to open the scoring against UTA Arad.

He then sprints towards the stand where Lauren and Darby are celebrating. He has just been a monster. But he is still a dad, in whatever language.

#1271. Cash In Immediately: Porro Wants to Leave Tottenham, Gray Is An Upgrade

Tottenham Hotspur saw their winning streak in the Premier League come to an end at Elland Road on Saturday afternoon as they fell to a 1-0 defeat against Leeds United.

Spurs headed into the game on the back of three consecutive victories, while Leeds had won just one of their last nine, but Noah Okafor's late strike was the difference between the two sides as the hosts took all three points to ease some of the pressure on Daniel Farke from the fans.

Tottenham, meanwhile, must now head back to the drawing board after a disappointing display which saw the manager apologise after the full-time whistle, with the north London side now sitting 11th in the table heading into the international break.

The game saw De Zerbi recall World Cup-winning full-back Pedro Porro to the starting lineup for the first time since the 3-2 defeat against Aston Villa back in September, with the Spaniard having recovered from a hamstring injury he suffered in that match.

But his performance against Leeds was disappointing to say the least. He completed just 67% of his passes in the game, was given a yellow card, didn't win a single aerial duel, committed three fouls, and won just half of his tackle attempts in the 65 minutes he was on the pitch.

It's worrying that his return coincided with a poor performance, especially when there has been speculation in recent weeks that he is keen to leave the club amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid, despite signing a new long-term contract before the World Cup.

Reports last month suggested that the player has lost faith in the project under De Zerbi and is seriously considering an exit in 2027. He has also since confirmed publicly that he wishes to return to Spain at some point in his career, admitting it was a "big dream".

“Obviously, I’d love to return to Spain someday. It’s my country, and I like the league. Right now, it would be very unfair to talk about anything other than my club because I’m under contract, but obviously, I’d love to go back to Spain; it’s a big dream of mine.”

Losing such an important member of the squad would be a blow, but Spurs got rid of Cristian Romero in the summer and haven't looked back, with Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi brought in to partner Micky Van de Ven instead.

Porro's departure would leave a hole in the squad that needs filling, but Spurs have already got a right-back option in the squad who fits the needs of De Zerbi's system even better than Porro does, and that is Archie Gray.

It's clear that Archie Gray is a key part of the Spurs squad under De Zerbi, even being included in the leadership group and wearing the captain's armband on occasion despite his tender age.

Playing either in central midfield or at right-back, the former Leeds sensation has established himself as an undroppable member of the squad this season, and the manager must find a way to continue giving him regular game time to help him develop.

While he may not be a better right-back than Porro in the traditional sense, he seems to fit the needs of De Zerbi's system better at this stage, and there would be no need to panic-buy a new right-back to replace Porro should he be sold. With the Spaniard having just signed a new contract, they could demand a huge fee to let him leave, and then put that towards addressing other areas of the squad that are in more urgent need, like the forward line.

It's unlikely to be a popular decision immediately, but if the board get the aftermath right then it will prove to be the perfect solution and something that can be looked back on fondly.

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

The 20-year-old, spoke about his rapid ascent to the top of the Italian pyramid in a recent interview with Cronache di Spohgliatoio.

Going back to where it all began, Cisse said: “My life changed when I was working in my father’s factory. A manager from Verona went to look for him to beg him to take me there. He’s always been a hard worker: Every day at 5 pm, he took a break from work and at 5:15 he’d be in front of the house calling me to take me to play football.

“I still remember the first time. It was in the afternoon, he came up to the house and said: ‘Come on, I’ve got somewhere to take you’. Then we went out onto the pitch. He was the one who passed down my passion for football, and from that moment, I’ve never stopped.”

Cisse feels that he still has plenty of growing up to do in a football sense, though.

“A few weeks ago they asked me how much of myself I’d shown as a footballer and I answered 70%. Maybe I have to lower that a little bit. Let’s say 40%, because I have to improve in many aspects. But, at the same time, I know who I am and what I’m worth.

“Last season Alberto Aquilani, who was my coach at Catanzaro, told me ‘if you don’t play for at least 10 years in Serie A, for me, you will have failed’. I took that as a positive piece of encouragement, and that sentence pushed me to do better and made me believe in the things I can do.”

There was plenty of young Italian talent in last season’s Catanzaro squad, including another fresh face in the Italy squad: Mattia Liberali. Costantino Favasuli also left Catanzaro to join Napoli over the summer.

“Favasuli is one of my best friends in football,” said Cisse. “I met him in Serie B last year. We often found ourselves talking and dreaming together. He once told me ;think about the day when we will be playing for two great teams. It would be great to play in Serie A, but I’m 23, maybe it’s too late for me’. But, he’s done it too. Milan vs. Napoli will be in December, so we’ll see how that goes.

“He was my driver, he would take me to training. He’s an example that there is no age limit to stop feeling young or to stop believing in yourself.”

Cisse went on to speak about the moment he found out he would be joining Milan during the January transfer window. He also had strong interest from Eredivisie side PSV at the time.

“My friends’ WhatsApp group exploded,” he recalled. “‘Alpha, is this true?,’ they were asking. And I said, ‘yeah guys, yes’. PSV wanted me immediately, but Milan were going to let me finish the season in Serie B. Two great teams, but Milan … you can’t describe it.

“It was a mix of emotions. My parents told me to stay calm and that the best was still yet to come. We decided that this was the right choice, and seeing how it’s going, I’d say we were right.”

PSV had been so close to signing Cisse, that he says he was “practically on the flight to Rotterdam to sign with PSV, but then Milan came in.”

Cisse’s first experiences with Milan came during the back end of the 2025-26 season, when he received treatment for an injury he picked up in Serie B.

“The first times I went to Milanello were for the injury recovery. Milan let me stay with Catanzaro, but I got injured a few days after. In fact, I had some big doubts: ‘I’m going to Milan after an injury, let’s see how it all goes’.

“This is exactly what Ruben Amorim spoke to me about when we first met. We focused on the injury, he explained what he wanted from me on the pitch. He’s a great person, who knows how to work with young people. And he knows how to keep my feet on the ground, even if I’m not one of those whose head is in the clouds.”

It has been a rapid rise to the top since then: Cisse is Milan’s leading goalscorer across all competitions with eight from 13 appearances, and their joint-top goalscorer in Serie A with five (from nine outings).

The first hat-trick of his career came in a 4-0 victory away against RB Salzburg in October.

“Everything felt clear to me after the hat-trick in the Europa League,” said Cisse. “It was confirmation of what I had thought to myself. It didn’t feel like I’d ‘arrived’, it was the realisation of a promise I’d made to myself as a child.

“Even though I was coming off a long injury, even though I’m young and still have a lot to improve, I’ve never had any doubts about my qualities and the places I could go. I’m very demanding of myself.

“My life has changed a lot over the last few months, maybe even more than I’ve realised myself. There are times when I stop and think about how different everything is compared to a short while ago. Football is taking me to places that I never could have dreamed of, but I’m still the same person inside.

“I know what my ambitions are and maybe that’s what helps me to not get lost in all of this, even when everything around you is changing.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

Very exciting young player. This is the way forward. Stop letting these talents go abroad for pennies. Give them opportunities here and now. Serie A needs more Cisse’s getting signed up and less examples like Issa Doumbia who all the bigs slept on and let get away. Last season alone really shows how much quality is in Serie B waiting to be given the chance to take the next step.

#1268. Liam Scales has no doubt 'amazing' Kasper Hogh will soon bring an end to his worrying Celtic goal drought

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:09 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 9 November 2026

Liam Scales claims he’s got no fears about Kasper Hogh’s luck turning after the Dane’s goalless run at Celtic extended to 16 matches.

Without a goal to his name since hitting a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, the forward thought his drought was over when he found the net against the same opponent on Sunday.

Denied his long-awaited moment of glory when VAR spotted an earlier infringement by Mika Baur, Hogh watched from the bench as Martin O’Neill’s side ground out a one-goal win which took them four points clear at the top of the table.

But while the Dane will now have to wait until the home match with St Mirren following the international break for his next opportunity, Scales – the scorer on the day – feels his team-mate has nothing to worry about.

‘He’s been brilliant,’ said the Irishman. ‘He keeps doing the right things and eventually it will fall for him.

‘He was so unlucky with his goal being ruled out. And he told me he was right behind me with the goal I scored. If I’d known that I might have left it!

Liam Scales was Celtic's weekend goal hero but he is tipping Kasper Hogh to come good

‘It will fall for him. He’s a goalscorer and a good player. His all-round game was brilliant, he held the ball up really well.

‘He’s just been unlucky. But his attitude has been brilliant. If he keeps doing the right things it will work out for him.

‘He has an amazing attitude and that’s why I really believe he will be successful.’

With Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty, O’Neill was grateful for the improvised finish of Scales earlier in the game.

‘It took an age to come down,’ Scales recalled of his third of the season. ‘I wasn’t sure if it was going to land on the roof of the net.

‘I was just trying to guide it on target and luckily enough it went in. It was nice to score and hopefully I can get a few more between now and the end of the season.’

The victory over Killie ensured Celtic bounced back from their loss at Falkirk and a draw with Dundee United and built on their dramatic midweek win over Besiktas in the Europa League.

‘It was definitely important,’ said Scales. ‘Two games without a win is bad enough, but three would have been a nightmare.

Hogh thought he had ended his scoring drought at Rugby Park but his effort was ruled out

‘We knew we needed that win and can go into the break and refresh. Some of the lads can rest and recover and hopefully we’ll come back in this form.

‘I do think confidence is a massive part of our group and it was probably hit a little bit. The win against a top side like Besiktas has boosted us a little bit. There’s kind of a better mood around and we just want to keep adding good results.’

Scales is optimistic that the better options that are now at the manager’s disposal can help the side hit the kind of form which has eluded them this season.

‘We had (Hyun-jun) Yang back on Sunday, Jota is obviously starting,’ he said. ‘These guys are getting back to full sharpness and getting minutes. Hopefully, this will help and we can build on it.

‘We know we haven’t been good enough between the last international window and this one. We’ve let a few results go and we’re not exactly where we want to be.

‘We always want to be on top of the table. We don’t want to be chasing. We want to be good arm’s length from the challengers.

‘Last season wasn’t what we wanted at all and we don’t want a repeat of that.’

#1266. Exclusive: Mikael Silvestre Names 'Very Special' England Star as Most Underrated Teammate

Former Manchester United, Arsenal, and France defender Mikael Silvestre has named the most underrated teammate from his playing career, while speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT.

The talented defender had an illustrious career in English football, making 275 appearances in the Premier League over 11 seasons, lifting the title five times, and also winning the Champions League, FA Cup and League Cup once.

He also had an excellent international career, winning the Confederations Cup twice and reaching the World Cup final in 2006, racking up 40 caps for Les Bleus between 2001 and 2006.

During those prime years of his career, Silvestre played alongside some legendary figures including Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney, Carlos Tevez, Ryan Giggs, Roy Keane, Zinedine Zidane, Thierry Henry, and Patrick Vieira.

At different points in his time at Old Trafford, Silvestre was the first-choice left-back and also the first-choice centre-back, showing his incredible versatility and quality, with Sir Alex Ferguson a huge fan of him after signing him from Inter Milan in 1999.

His experience and quality convinced Arsene Wenger to take him to the Emirates Stadium when his time at Man Utd came to an end, which allowed him to continue his career in England and play alongside some more top stars such as Cesc Fabregas, Samir Nasri, and Robin van Persie.

But while speaking to GIVEMESPORT, via Action Network, a prediction market publisher covering Polymarket offers, Silvestre was asked to name the most underrated teammate of his playing career, and he didn't hesitate when providing his answer.

“Paul Scholes was underrated. Obviously, he got his flowers at Man Utd but for England and outside of Man Utd he wasn't rated as high as he should be in my opinion.

“He was a top, top player, and being his teammate in training, he was a very special talent.”

Scholes was part of the Man Utd squad for the entirety of Silvestre's time at Old Trafford, and is widely regarded as one of the club's best ever players. The midfield playmaker made 718 appearances for Man Utd during his career, winning 11 Premier League titles, three FA Cups, two League Cups, and two Champions League titles.

But outside of Manchester, his reputation is not as esteemed as you would think, with his quiet nature in the public eye during his playing days likely going against him.

Considering some of the talent that Silvestre played alongside, it's no surprise that the former England midfielder, one of the greatest midfielders of the Premier League era, is likely seen as underrated.

But Scholes is often heralded by his peers, and was recently described as the best player in Premier League history by Thierry Henry, who also felt the iconic midfielder was underrated.

"I don't think people have given him the credit he deserves. (He's) one of the best, if not the best, I've played against, he could do anything. Unfortunately for him, when he was playing for the national team, for England, sometimes people didn't see it like that."

The England star made an interesting choice.

#1265. Golden Boy Award 2026 goes to Cubarsi, with Ahanor Best Italian

Barcelona and Spain defender Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, with Erling Haaland named Golden Player, Honest Ahanor Italian Golden Boy and Arsenal’s Italian Andrea Berta Best Executive.

The awards were announced today at the Mapei Football Center, marking the latest chapter in the history of the competition set up by Turin-based newspaper Tuttosport.

It was created in 2003 and assigned to the best Under-21 player in European football, voted for by a jury of 50 journalists from around the continent.

Previous winners include Lionel Messi, Cesc Fabregas, Wayne Rooney, Alexandre Pato, Mario Balotelli, Paul Pogba, Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Lamine Yamal.

Cubarsí makes history as the first defender since Matthijs de Ligt in 2018 to win the Golden Boy award, he follows in the footsteps of last year’s winner Désiré Doué of France and Paris Saint-Germain.

Since 2018, there are also other categories in the Golden Boy awards to spread beyond the traditional remit.

Manchester City’s Haaland has been named Golden Player, with former Atalanta defender Ahanor, who is now on loan at Crystal Palace via Chelsea, received the award for Italian Golden Boy.

Giulia Galli is Best Italian Golden Girl, Felicia Schroder is European Golden Girl, and Alessia Russo of England and Arsenal is Golden Player Woman.

Barcelona’s Joan Laporta was named Best President, Arsenal’s Italian chief Andrea Berta is Best Executive, and Jorge Mendes Best Agent.

#1264. What Has Happened to Vozinha and His Family Since the World Cup

Vozinha became one of the breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup, but the Cape Verde goalkeeper has admitted he would rather have his old life back.

The 40-year-old was one of the more unexpected stars after making seven saves in a 0-0 draw with eventual champions Spain in Cape Verde's first-ever World Cup match, and went on to help the island nation reach the knockout stage.

His Instagram following jumped from 56,000 to more than a million by the end of the Spain game, after Brazilian broadcaster CazéTV encouraged its audience to follow him, yet it has proven to be a difficult time.

Speaking to The Observer, Vozinha explained how dramatically his life has changed.

Cristiano Ronaldo gained over 11 million social media followers during the World Cup... but that's not even close to number one.

He added: "To be honest, if I were offered the life I have today or the life I had before, I'd choose the one I had before."

The attention has spread to his family. The Observer reports that supporters turn up at his mother's home in Cape Verde every day, asking for photos or a chat. "I'm not there, so I can't help them," Vozinha said. "They have to learn to live with the situation and set boundaries."

On the pitch, things have not been straightforward either. Vozinha was a free agent at the time of his fame, and opted to leave Portuguese second-tier side Chaves to join Chilean giants Colo-Colo after the tournament, but his deal only runs until the end of 2026.

According to Chilean outlets La Tercera and Emol, the contract extends automatically for another year only if he plays at least half of the club's available minutes. If he falls short, Colo-Colo can let him leave at no cost. He has kept clean sheets, but has faced criticism over his handling.

His return to international duty also went badly. Vozinha was at fault for Mali's third goal in a 3-1 defeat in 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying, coming off his line poorly and leaving the ball loose for Dorgeles Nene to score.

Spanish newspaper AS described the result as a "golpe de realidad", a reality check, for Cape Verde. As Frank Sinatra sang, that's life.

The two players were seen in conversation after the match.

Just weeks after missing out on the Yashin Award at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, Vozinha proved he's still got plenty to give to the sport. In November, the veteran helped Colo Colo to the Chilean title.

After sealing the trophy, the Cape Verde international dedicated the triumph to his family and country. He said: "Today is a day for celebrating; we'll talk about the future later. This title is for my entire family and for Cape Verde."

#1263. Falkirk boss John McGlynn deserves big move, says Craig Levein, as Aberdeen sack Stephen Robinson

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 9 November 2026

Craig Levein believes John McGlynn ‘ticks every box’ to manage a bigger club than Falkirk — as Aberdeen begin the search for Stephen Robinson’s successor.

The Northern Irishman was sacked last night after eight months in charge, with the Dons’ 4-0 home loss to Hibs on Saturday proving to be the last straw.

With the Pittodrie side now sitting second bottom of the Premiership, chairman Dave Cormack, sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel and newly-appointed chief executive Adrian Bevington will soon begin the process of trying to identify the man they believe can take the team forward.

And Levein, a former Hearts colleague of McGlynn’s, believes the veteran’s record of taking the Bairns from League One to third place in the top flight should speak for itself.

'John has passed every test that’s been put in front of him and I don’t know what he needs to do,’ said Levein.

‘Falkirk supporters, of course, won’t like me saying that, but I’ve worked with the guy. He’s got integrity, knowledge, he delves into the minutiae when he’s doing his team talks and makes sure everybody knows what’s expected.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn has guided them from League One to third in the Premiership

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson was sacked after eight months in charge at Pittodrie

‘I’m biased, I like the guy, but I think he’s done a wonderful job. He’s done all the work that he needs to do in my eyes to get an opportunity.’

McGlynn worked at Hearts as a coach under Jim Jefferies and went on to manage the Gorgie club twice — once as an interim.

Prior to taking charge of Falkirk in 2022, he had two spells at Raith Rovers, a stint at Livingston and a scouting role at Celtic under Brendan Rodgers.

Despite completely turning the Bairns’ fortunes around, Levein believes that there remains a strange reluctance in some quarters to recognise the 64-year-old as one of the shrewdest managers in the country.

‘I don’t know what it is, looking at what he’s done, his whole body of work,’ shrugged Levein.

‘When I went to Hearts at the tail end of my career, I was helping John do some training with the youngsters. Even then, you could tell immediately that he knows what he’s talking about.

‘He spent a fair bit of time with Brendan at Celtic. After that, I think he adopted Brendan’s style of football with some changes and altered two or three bits.

‘Essentially, he went to Celtic, watched and learned everything on top of the knowledge he already had. His team at Raith started to play in the same way as Celtic did. Then he’s continued that when he’s gone to Falkirk.

‘I was promoting him for the Scotland job when it came around. If you look at his record, it’s pretty impressive.

‘I just think he is undervalued, maybe not by the supporters that have had him as their manager, but certainly in a wider sense in Scotland. He has done a brilliant job so far.

‘I’ll come back to the fact I’m biased. I like the guy. I like what he does at football clubs. If I’m a chairman, all day long I’d be looking for somebody like him.

‘He’s meticulous in his work and everything’s done properly. He stays within the bandwidth of emotions.

‘He doesn’t get overly emotional during matches and he stays in his area, which I think is good for him and good for his players.

‘You don’t often see him throwing stuff about in the dugout or anything like that. He’s a top manager who has improved enormously in the last five or six years.’

Craig Levein believes McGlynn has done more than enough to merit a move to a bigger club

Robinson’s departure was confirmed yesterday in a statement.

Despite winning the League Cup with St Mirren a year ago and guiding the Buddies to three straight top-six finishes, he never enjoyed a consistent run of results at Pittodrie.

‘Following a board meeting, Aberdeen Football Club has today taken the decision to part company with head coach Stephen Robinson,’ the statement read.

‘Stephen leaves the club alongside assistant head coach Brian Kerr and first team coach Stephen Craigan. We thank them for their efforts during their time at Pittodrie and wish them every success for the future.

‘Preparatory work to support the appointment of a new manager has been undertaken, and the recruitment process is ongoing. The focus will be on identifying the right candidate to lead the club forward and deliver the progress expected across all areas of the football operation.

‘Stuart Duff will assume interim charge of first team training while the club continues its search for a new head coach.’

#1262. Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

“It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”
