#1247. Fleetwood knock out Arsenal in one of biggest shocks in League Cup history

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

Eighty-four rungs separated these teams at kick-off, but, now and again, you get a situation when the floodlights are on, belief is high and the sense of history is prevalent. It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

Having chiselled out a 1-1 draw in 90 minutes in which Max Dowman was sent off, Fleetwood dispatched five nerveless spot-kicks, the last one thundered in by Conor Haughey after Bruno Guimarães’s penalty was saved by Jay Lynch.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”

This was ignominious for Arsenal, an elimination from this tournament to rival the 1969 loss in the final to Swindon Town or the 2012 exit to Bradford, then also of League Two. What made this so astonishing was the fact that Mikel Arteta went so strong.

You should never be surprised by anything these days, but, even still, an eight-minute delay because of a drone flying over this wonderful little venue would not have been on anyone’s bingo card. Only 57 seconds had been played when Michael Salisbury, the referee, saw a light in the sky and said “stop”.

A drone stops play at the Highbury Stadium. https://t.co/TvjNjjACFM

The precaution was understandable. Only 10 days ago, one idiot escaped from a village to kick a rugby ball off the roof of an apartment block into the Gtech Community Stadium while Brentford and Liverpool were playing and could have caused serious injury.

So while the locals harrumphed as the players tried to keep themselves warm, no risk could be taken. Eventually, police apprehended the operator in a nearby park. It was something unfathomable, which was also true of what happened when the contest resumed.

The anticipation was that Arsenal would saunter clear against opponents who had lost at Exeter City on Saturday, leaving them 18th in England’s fourth tier. But it only took a few skirmishes to appreciate this was not going to be the cakewalk anticipated in what was the biggest occasion in Fleetwood’s history.

Arteta absolutely knew his team were not operating at the levels they should have been. He was wrapped up against the elements in a thick black jacket but, every so often, he would express his exasperation at Jurriën Timber, captain for the night, to “get forward!”

They were in a battle, that much was obvious, and one challenge from Shaun Rooney – so forceful you thought the ball might burst – sent Myles Lewis-Skelly spinning like a top. How Fleetwood’s fans loved it, roaring their approval as the young England international hit the ground with a thump.

Arsenal had one good chance when Dowman skipped down the right and dragged a shot across the box that Viktor Gyökeres could not divert but then, wonderfully, things took a totally unexpected turn when Fleetwood poked their noses in front.

It was a League Two goal in its simplicity, but that is no criticism. Harrison Neal helped a long ball forward, putting it behind Marli Salmon and Aaron Loupalo-Bi relished the chance to get into a foot race, grappling with the England Under-17 international.

Salmon looked like he had him at one point, but Loupalo-Bi was strong – not to mention composed – and he held off the challenge to slide a left-footed shot through the legs of Illan Meslier, who was making his Arsenal debut. What followed was unique to the magic of an English cup tie.

Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Eberechi Eze are among the players stepping off the bus, so at the very least it will be a strong bench.

Aside from their stadium being called Highbury, Fleetwood Town’s red shirts with white sleeves also bear a striking resemblance to Arsenal’s home kit. The club in its current guise was founded in 1997, although previous iterations date back to 1908 under the name Fleetwood FC.

There is no evidence or anecdote suggesting Arsenal were the inspiration, so it appears the kit clash is a coincidence. Arsenal will be wearing their navy away strip.

The club’s most famous son is surely Jamie Vardy, who scored 31 goals in 36 appearances for Fleetwood in the 2011-12 season before Leicester City made their move.

An unfamiliar opponent at a very familiar sounding venue, Arsenal play Fleetwood Town for the first time this evening at the Lancashire club’s Highbury Stadium.

Fleetwood, 18th in League Two, are the lowest-ranked team remaining in this season’s League Cup, having booked their place in the fourth round thanks to a victory at Sheffield United.

They were playing in English football’s sixth tier in 2009, and so while their stadium may share its name with Arsenal’s former home, the two clubs are worlds apart.

The League Cup is fourth of four competitions on Arsenal’s list of priorities, but Mikel Arteta should be able to rotate extensively while progressing to the quarter-finals. With a trip to Anfield on Sunday, that is a welcome luxury.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Cristhian Mosquera, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres are seasoned internationals in need of minutes and in line to start.

Max Dowman lit up Arsenal’s third-round victory at Ipswich Town, and 17-year-old centre-back Marli Salmon was not far behind him. Young striker and Northern Ireland international Ceadach O’Neill is also expected to be involved, and he may be joined by other academy players.

While attention is fixed on Premier League and Champions League success, Arsenal’s stinging defeat by Manchester City in last season’s final of this competition will not have been forgotten by Arteta or his players.

Matt Lawlor, Fleetwood’s manager, was full of praise for Arsenal in his pre-match press conference: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch. The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.

“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

Arteta has told his players that they must keep their standards high, with a lack of concentration or professionalism potentially their worst enemy against fourth-tier opposition.

Arteta said: “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve that, and then try to win and try to play a bit better than them.“We know the risk, and in football, things can get very equal the moment you are able to match certain things, and that’s why our basics and habits have to be through the roof to be able to win the game.”Full team news on the way shortly.

#1246. Napoli draw up Allegri wish list for big January spending

Max Allegri has reportedly requested four January reinforcements to break out of Napoli’s crisis, including a right-back, a physical midfielder, and two strikers, as Noa Lang and Lorenzo Lucca are expected to leave.

The Partenopei are struggling badly in both Serie A and the Champions League, but while many are calling for the dismissal of Allegri, it seems President Aurelio De Laurentiis is prepared to give his coach a boost instead.

La Gazzetta dello Sport suggest that Allegri has asked for four specific roles to bolster the squad, with some intriguing names mentioned.

Especially after Giovanni Di Lorenzo’s injury, they are lacking a genuine right-back, as Costantino Favasuli is more of a wing-back figure than working hard in defence.

The name put forward by the report is Vinicius Tobias, currently at Shakhtar Donetsk and who played in the 1-0 Champions League defeat to Inter last month.

In midfield, an alternative to the physicality of Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa is required, although AS Monaco’s Mamadou Coulibaly is going to be too expensive at circa €40m, so Darryl Bakola at Sassuolo is a cheaper option.

Finally, it is widely reported that both Lang and Lucca will be leaving again, as neither managed to win back the support of the fans after ill-fated loan experiences last season.

This means two forwards are required, most notably someone who can be a centre-forward in the vein of Rasmus Hojlund.

The top target is Monza hitman Gustavo Varela, who has just earned his first senior Portugal call after nine goals in his first 10 Serie A appearances, plus two in a single Coppa Italia match.

#1245. Simeone equals Luis Aragonés’s LaLiga wins record as Atlético Madrid beat Levante 2-0

Atlético Madrid won 2-0 at Levante on Saturday, making it a milestone afternoon for Diego Simeone. Barcelona are next up in the league, and one more victory would give him the coaching record on his own.

Atlético Madrid’s trip to Valencia ended with a milestone for their coach. It took the Argentine 565 LaLiga matches in charge to reach the mark, according to Club Atlético de Madrid.

The visitors went in at the interval a goal up. Álex Baena supplied the pass for their second. Earlier, Morten Hjulmand had a goal ruled out by VAR in the 17th minute. Levante coach Luís Castro was shown a yellow card for dissent a minute later.

The scoreline did not reflect the balance of chances. Levante shot 14 times from inside the box, while Atlético managed 3. The hosts’ expected goals reached 1.33, against 0.63 for the visitors.

Jan Oblak was the difference. Around the tenth minute, he made a crucial one-handed save to deny Dani Requena, Infobae (EFE) reported. The goalkeeper finished with a rating of 8.08.

Atlético had more of the ball, with 54% possession and 560 passes to Levante’s 450. Simeone made two double changes. Jonathan David and Sørloth replaced Lee Kang-In and Julián Álvarez in the 67th minute. Le Normand and Lookman came on for Barrios and Baena in the 76th.

The result was Atlético’s seventh league win in a row. It briefly took them top of the table. The teams’ last meeting, on 31 January 2026, had ended 0-0 in Valencia.

Simeone already leads Aragonés on wider measures at the club. Across all official competitions with Atlético, he has 479 wins from 813 games. Aragonés managed 308 wins from 612 games there. The club credits Simeone with eight trophies as coach, two more than Aragonés’s six.

The coming weeks carry real weight. From 11 games, Atlético have nine wins, one draw and one defeat. Real Madrid sit third on 24 points from 10 games.

Three big points in Valencia 💪 pic.twitter.com/W1JUeW8Uqh

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) October 31, 2026

Levante are 17th on 10 points after their second straight defeat. They travel to Tarancón in the Copa del Rey on Thursday 5 November. Their next league game is away to Celta de Vigo at 18:30 on Sunday 8 November.

Atlético host Bayern München in the Champions League on Tuesday 3 November. Their meeting with Barcelona is the last match of matchday 12, kicking off at 21:00 on Sunday 8 November. The Riyadh Air Metropolitano will stage the game.

#1244. Chelsea Confidential: Mike Penders' Vaseline goalkeeping hack revealed, Emi Martinez fitness update, why Estevao started against 'weak' Man United and the £750 'dressing room experience' for Blues fans

Published: 07:03 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 14:51 EST, 4 November 2026

One of the secrets to Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders stopping Manchester United from scoring at Stamford Bridge was to smear a stash of Vaseline on his goalpost.

The 21-year-old Belgian used the petroleum jelly to add grip to his gloves during the game and particularly before corners. Prior to one United set-piece, Penders walked to the woodwork to rub his hands with the substance which was hidden up high towards his crossbar. He then caught the ball when Bruno Fernandes’ cross came into his box.

It seems counterintuitive to smear a greasy substance on gloves to aid catching but it is an old goalkeeper hack – and perfectly legal in the laws of the game – with former England keeper Ben Foster once saying on his podcast: ‘It’s hard to explain, but if we were in a training session, I could tell you if one of us had Vaseline on our gloves, because as soon as I grab the ball, it does make it grippier.’

Penders may have learned the trick from Sweden’s Karl-Johan Johnsson. They were both at Chelsea’s sister side Strasbourg last season – Penders as No 1 and Johnsson as No 2.

Johnsson is now 36 and without a club. He did not respond when contacted by Confidential, but he does have an old YouTube channel. His most popular video – viewed 54,000 times and uploaded in 2021 when he was a goalkeeper for Copenhagen – is about the benefits of Vaseline.

While Johnsson would apply it from the blue-topped tub in the changing room before kick-off, he would also add a chunk to his goalpost so he could easily top up mid-match if needed.

Mike Penders has a novel trick he uses to help keep the ball out of the Chelsea net

Penders saves Ryan Gravenberch's penalty kick in the Carabao Cup shootout against Liverpool at Anfield

The Vaseline tip has tended to be passed on from ‘keeper to ‘keeper. Ask Foster and he will say he learned it from Joe Hart. Ask Hart and he will credit Kasper Schmeichel. And so on.

For Johnsson, he believes there is a psychological benefit as it not only gave greater grip to his gloves but made him feel more confident in goal, particularly in wet weather.

Stamford Bridge was soaking when Penders struggled in his first Premier League start as Tottenham Hotspur visited Chelsea. That was a match played in the midst of Storm Boelo. At one corner, the youngster filling in for Emiliano Martinez mistimed a punch for an own goal. With that lead, Spurs went on to win 2-0, their first victory at the Bridge since 2018.

It is not known if Penders used the Vaseline hack in that derby defeat, but sources told Confidential to look out for his use of it in their following two fixtures versus Liverpool and United.

Penders put in a fine performance at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, despite Chelsea losing on penalties at Anfield after a 1-1 draw. Had Emmanuel Emegha scored his spot-kick, Xabi Alonso’s side would have reached the quarter-finals after Penders denied Ryan Gravenberch from 12 yards.

In Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League victory over United, Penders made sure of his clean sheet with several saves, including a world-class stop as he tipped Bryan Mbeumo’s rocket on to his crossbar.

As mentioned, the hack is entirely legal. IFAB – football’s lawmakers – have no rule against Vaseline or any other petroleum jelly being applied to goalkeepers’ gloves in their regulations on player equipment.

Penders saves from Liverpool's Ronald Araujo during the Carabao Cup match

Penders punches a slippery ball into his own net against Tottenham on a miserable evening at Stamford Bridge

In more goalkeeper news, Martinez has been privately pushing to play in Chelsea’s trip to Sunderland this Sunday, per sources who also revealed how he has been insisting to club colleagues that he wants to represent Argentina during the upcoming international break.

Since this information was relayed to Confidential earlier this week, Martinez has indeed been called up by Lionel Scaloni for his country’s friendlies versus Uruguay and Costa Rica. He is also understood to have returned to Chelsea training on Wednesday, albeit with strapping around his jaw.

Alonso confirmed at his last press conference that ‘there is a chance’ his goalkeeper could return before the break. That would leave Chelsea’s manager with a decision to make – whether to stick with Penders, who has shown his potential in the last two games, or turn to Martinez, who has seen a specialist while sidelined about having a face-mask fitted.

The 34-year-old broke his jaw in Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League win away at Everton in mid-October. He had surgery, and said at the time that he would be ‘back in a few weeks’. That will be three weeks ago this weekend when Alonso’s squad travel to Sunderland.

Meanwhile, Aaron Anselmino has also been called up by Argentina, despite having not played a single minute for Chelsea this season. He has only made the match-day squad once as an unused substitute in their first game in the Carabao Cup against Luton Town in August.

Then he disappeared. But Confidential did spy Anselmino last Saturday for the first time in a while as he took a seat behind the bench, and now he is in Scaloni's squad. That is despite Alonso telling us at his last press conference that he was injured.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez breaks his jaw in a clash with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite last month

Marintez receives treatment on the Hill Dickinson Stadium turf - but is pushing for a return to action this weekend

SUNDERLAND WOULD PREFER PENDERS OVER MARTINEZ

Confidential asked former Sunderland striker Kevin Phillips whether he would rather face Penders or Martinez.

The 53-year-old, who scored 92 Premier League goals, told us: ‘The obvious one would be Penders, with his lack of experience, coming to the Stadium of Light, which is going to be a hostile, noisy occasion.

‘Emiliano, he's got the experience, played an awful long time at Villa. Obviously, he's had his injury, but he's an experienced international, been there, seen it and done it. So you would say Penders for his inexperience. But it looks like Martinez might be the one who starts, with a mask on, which, from Sunderland's point of view, means you're going to have to test him.’

Phillips spoke to us via Best Betting Sites and when asked if Martinez’s recent injury would impact Sunderland’s approach if he is in goal, he said: ‘The natural one with Martinez is that nobody wants to go and hurt him again. It's a terrible injury, so you don't want a recurrence.

‘So anything physical, no. But from a wide point of view, getting the ball in the box, from set-plays, put the ball in high, just to see if he's confident to come for crosses, come and punch it. That would be my advice, certainly not to get physical with him.

‘Take every opportunity to shoot. Put him under pressure early and see how he copes. But from Chelsea's point of view, if he wasn't 100 per cent, they wouldn't risk him.’

Chelsea sources who were consulted by Confidential after Estevao was suddenly handed his first Premier League start of the season have explained why Manchester United were deliberately picked as the opponents.

We are told Alonso has had concerns about the 19-year-old Brazilian’s physicality and Chelsea’s fitness staff have been tasked with working on building him up. But United, managed by Michael Carrick, were seen as ideal opposition for him to face from the beginning.

United were considered weaker than the Premier League's other physical sides, which lessened Alonso’s reservations. Estevao did indeed have fun, could not be tamed by Diogo Dalot, and was unfortunate not to get among the goals in the 2-0 win.

It remains to be seen if Estevao will now keep his place away at Sunderland, where Chelsea crumbled on the final day of last season to end up out of Europe.

Estevao (left) was given a rare start against Manchester United at the weekend when he teamed up nicely with Morgan Rogers

There were some interesting quotes from Regis Le Bris last week as the Sunderland boss praised his centre back Omar Alderete after they beat Brentford in the Carabao Cup.

'We spoke about the style of play,’ Le Bris said. ‘We try to press high. It’s more or less the trend of the Premier League. You press up, and it means your opponent will go long. If your centre backs are not strong, consistent and able to manage one v ones, it’s over. Thank you, Omar.’

Except, Alderete is now suspended for the visit of Chelsea, and despite Le Bris liking to press high, the statistics say only Coventry have won possession in the final third fewer times than Sunderland this season.

It is a big game for Le Bris, who has avoided losing his job while his side sit bottom of the Premier League with a vote of confidence coming from his board in the build-up to Chelsea’s visit.

This weekend's Chelsea match is a big one for Regis Le Bris, the under-pressure Sunderland manager

Chelsea are making significant money on having fans lay out their favourite player’s kit and boots in the changing room on a matchday, while the supporter can also leave a good-luck message.

The ‘VVIP dressing room experience’ is already a sell-out for Chelsea’s next Premier League home game versus Leeds United on Saturday, November 21 at £750 per person.

There are other perks which come with that package – you aren’t just paying to do the kit-man’s job for him – but it is another example of Chelsea’s outside-of-the-box hospitality ideas.

#1243. Report Hermoso ready to sign new Roma contract

Mario Hermoso is reportedly in advanced negotiations to extend his contract with Roma for up to another three years, as he would be a free agent at the end of this season.

The 31-year-old arrived on a free transfer in the summer of 2024, but after a difficult first season was sent out on loan to Bayer Leverkusen.

He has been a rock in the defence since returning to the Stadio Olimpico, also scoring three goals in 14 games between Serie A and the Champions League.

The Spaniard’s current contract only runs to June 2026, but Sky Sport Italia reporter Angelo Mangiante is confident negotiations are in full swing for an extension.

It is expected to be for two years, with an option for a third added in, and could be signed as early as next month.

A product of the Real Madrid youth academy, Hermoso went on to make his name at Real Valladollid, Espanyol and above all Atletico Madrid, where he remained for five years.

#1241. Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out

Unfortunately for Chelsea, Wesley Fofana put his hand up twice. Firstly to concede the first-half penalty for handball that allowed Liverpool to equalise quickly after Chelsea themselves had scored from the spot.

And secondly to volunteer to take one of the penalties in the shoot-out. The defender had to score to keep Chelsea in it, but he woefully, nervously skied his effort high into a gleeful Kop and it was Liverpool who went through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

LIVERPOOL ARE THROUGH TO THE QUARTER-FINALS OF THE CARABAO CUP! 🔴 Wesley Fofana blazes over to hand Liverpool their FIFTH consecutive victory ✅ https://t.co/M4n01R8DSk

There the reward for Andoni Iraola, the head coach, is a home tie against the club he left in the summer: Bournemouth. The draw has opened up for Liverpool, and they know it, with only Manchester City left of the other big guns. But despite again playing at Anfield, they would have preferred not to face such a dangerous and motivated opponent, who have just reeled off five wins and five clean sheets in a row under Iraola’s replacement, Marco Rose.

This was also a big win. A meaningful win. One that was celebrated as such with Dua Lipa’s One Kiss – an anthem on Jürgen Klopp’s run to Liverpool’s first Champions League final under him in 2018 – played over the loudspeakers at the end as the players joyfully milled around the pitch.

One kiss is all it takes 🎶 https://t.co/0jfujy4V94

“I am happy to feel it. We feel the support,” Iraola said when asked whether he sensed the momentum and togetherness building in his reshaped Liverpool side. It looks as though they are.

Fofana was Chelsea’s eighth taker, so they were running out of options, but it was a truly terrible effort. The 25-year-old turned and scratched his head – just as many Chelsea fans have done over his underwhelming, albeit injury-hit, contributions since his eyebrow-raising £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.

Both sides had the chance to win it earlier in the shoot-out. For Liverpool it was Kostas Tsimikas, who had taken the decisive kick to beat Chelsea in a shoot-out in the 2022 FA Cup final, but the Greek full-back also completely missed the target.

Tsimikas has the chance to put Liverpool through... And fires over the bar! 😱 https://t.co/eCKBT6njMB

Then Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha – on his debut – saw his kick saved, after an effort by Ryan Gravenberch had also been stopped. In the end, Liverpool’s stand-in captain Joe Gomez – still to score an actual goal – crashed in his kick before Fofana’s blunder. The 29-year-old Gomez finally “scored” and it was an assured strike.

This was the fifth penalty shoot-out between these two clubs, in all competitions, with Liverpool having now triumphed in all five. They won the toss for this one and elected to take the kicks in front of the Kop, which roared its satisfaction and did its best to unsettle the Chelsea takers.

Both stand-in goalkeepers – Giorgi Mamardashvili and Mike Penders – made one outstanding save each in the shoot-out. Chelsea substitute Valentín Barco was the other player to miss, hitting a post.

Chelsea blink first in the shootout! 🔵 Valentín Barco's penalty bounces off the post... https://t.co/rSXGfQctbI

The other efforts, in truth, were outstanding and assured with Liverpool, undoubtedly, benefitting from Iraola turning to his bench and bringing on Alexander Isak, Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. All scored their penalties.

Among Chelsea’s scorers was Jordan Henderson and the former Liverpool captain received a strange homecoming in his first appearance at Anfield for three years. He was booed, in the first half at least, and especially when he tucked the ball under his arm before Chelsea took their penalty – in normal time – which gave them the lead. Henderson turned to the stands, grinning.

Morgan Rogers buries the spotkick! ⚽️ Chelsea take the lead at Anfield 🔵 https://t.co/YlDn2gakRi

In truth it was more pantomime than meaningful and Henderson, like another former, Champions League-winning Liverpool midfielder Xabi Alonso – now Chelsea’s head coach – did not celebrate as Morgan Rogers scored. There is no VAR at this stage of the competition but referee Darren England appeared to get all the big calls right. Rogers claimed a penalty before Chelsea’s one was awarded, but Ronald Araújo was probably just too strong.

Caicedo puts Tsimikas’ cross from the left behind for the first corner of the night. Gakpo sends in the inswinger but the whistle goes as Chelsea are awarded a free-kick for a foul from Tsimikas on Gusto.

#1239. Alisson, 34, reveals he wants to STAY at Liverpool after rolling back the years against Crystal Palace... but is extending the goalkeeper's contract the right call, asks LEWIS STEELE

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:06 EST, 9 November 2026

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker insists he wants to stay at the club after his contract expires at the end of this season.

The Brazilian, now 34, put in a throwback performance in the Reds’ win at Crystal Palace on Sunday with some fine stops to keep his side in the game at 0-0 before the big-money attackers did their job at the other end.

It came after a period where Alisson has been questioned by fans for a string of errors in what is his final contracted year at the club. And the No1 has now opened up on his future for the first time.

Asked if he wants to stay beyond the end of the season, Alisson said: ‘Yes, in my mind. I’m focused on playing every game but in my mind I’m happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

‘But my will is to stay. I’m happy here, my family is happy here. I’m still hungry for titles and for delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that’s my thinking on that.’

Alisson later added that his agent has held talks with the club over a new deal.

The 34-year-old keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window

The keeper will spend the next week resting after not being called up by Brazil for the second straight international window, which he admits is a decision taken somewhat beyond his will.

He said: ‘It is beneficial (not going), for sure. You have to use it right because you have a lot of time so if you don’t train, if you don’t prepare, time goes really quick and you need to stay sharp.

‘It’s not that I will sit on the couch for a week and then come back training. I still have to work hard but in my mind I can use the time to relax and be more with my family.

‘It’s a little bit against my will. What I always want is to be with the national team but I understand this is what I have at the moment and I will use this time and take the benefit from the rest.’

Should Liverpool continue in Alisson wonderland?

It is tempting to just say ‘yes’ and end this debate there.

Alisson is still the best goalkeeper Liverpool have on their books and, even though he is maybe not as solid as he once was, the 34-year-old remains one of the best goalkeepers in the world.

Last summer, he flirted with the idea of leaving and seriously considered a move to Juventus. Alisson speaks fluent Italian from his time at AS Roma and held talks with the Turin club over a return.

But Liverpool triggered a clause in his deal to extend his stay by a year. With several big names leaving such as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson, Ibrahima Konate and Curtis Jones, the club did not want another experienced head to depart and leave a leadership vacuum.

They have also spent the last three years succession planning for Alisson’s long-term replacement and have signed a number of goalkeepers for more than £60million combined.

Giorgi Mamardashvili is the most obvious in the pecking order. He has had mixed reviews with fans but the Georgian is appreciated more internally than maybe externally. The club believes he has several levels left to step up.

Lucca Brughmans will join from Belgian side Genk after a £28.3million deal was struck. Liverpool genuinely think he is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him.

Liverpool think Lucca Brughmans - who will join them from Belgian side Genk - is the best goalkeeper on the market and they fought off stiff competition from Real Madrid to sign him

They have also signed highly-rated Armin Pecsi and England youth goalkeeper Zach Trinder from Wolves.

Clearly, the post-Alisson future is sorted, with some of them tipped to go far in the game. But are any of them better than Alisson now? No. Will any of them be better next season? No.

Alisson missed 54 games across the previous two seasons with injury and illness, according to Transfermarkt, but his omission from Brazil camps and a specialised pre-season programme mean the keeper seems to have put his issues behind him. Touch wood.

For that reason, a one-year extension makes sense – for both Alisson and 35-year-old captain Virgil van Dijk. The club will have to face up to a future without both of their defensive stalwarts but, for now, they remain the best in class.

#1238. Baldini: ‘Chivu and Fabregas good for Italian football, not afraid to play youth’

Italy Under-21 coach Silvio Baldini insists ‘there are no friendly games’ at international level, while Cesc Fabregas and Cristian Chivu ‘are good for football, because they teach and are not afraid to play youth.’

The Azzurrini secured qualification for the European Under-21 Championship, which will be played next summer.

Meanwhile, they have two prestigious friendly tests against France on Friday November 13, and Belgium on November 16.

“As I always tell the lads, there are no friendly games when you are representing the Nazionale, because when you wear the Azzurri shirt, you carry the honour and pride of our country, our culture and our roots,” said Baldini in his press conference.

“We cannot think that we are playing friendly matches. We need to give our best every time, as if it was an official competitive game.”

Baldini had for two games been the interim Italy coach when Gennaro Gattuso resigned in the wake of the World Cup play-off failure, but has returned to his main role with the Under-21 side.

“Youth is vital for our football, and I embraced this role with so much enthusiasm. I also want to thank the media, because you spoke a lot about the fact Italian football was in a tunnel, and the only way to get out of it was to make reforms and have more courage in using young players.

“The responses we’ve seen have been positive at club level. I think of Chivu at Inter and Fabregas at Como, talented coaches who are good for football, because they know how to teach players, they set rules, and are not afraid to play youth.

“This is a spell where coaches like this give a big contribution to the development of Italian football, so we are fortunate they are working here in Serie A. Now I hope that others follow their example.”

Several of the Italy Under-21 talents have been promoted to the senior squad for the final two Nations League games against France and Belgium.

They include Milan forward Alphadjo Cisse, Como’s Mattia Liberali, Parma striker Simone Lontani and Crystal Palace defender Honest Ahanor.

Brentford talent Michael Kayode had already made the step up along with Sporting midfielder Issa Doumbia and Roma’s Niccolò Pisilli.

Fabián Ruiz scored twice as Paris Saint-Germain beat Villarreal 6-0 at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Tuesday 3 November 2026. The visitors led 4-0 at the break in round four of the Champions League league stage.

João Neves opened the scoring in the ninth minute. Désiré Doué added a second three minutes later from a Maghnes Akliouche pass. Senny Mayulu struck in the 13th minute. Ruiz then converted another Akliouche assist.

#1235. Xabi Alonso was brought in to end the chaos at Chelsea and he is failing. PLUS: Football's most vanilla pundit gives out-of-his-depth Michael Carrick an easy ride: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:55 EST, 9 November 2026

The whiff of Premier League failure is in the air as the smoke clears from Bonfire Night.

It always feels this way by the time we get to the November international break.

Managers and their players have had time to settle in and teething problems no longer cut it as a reason for autumn struggles.

Worst of all, Christmas is coming and we all know what tends to happen to teams who are struggling as the end of the year nears.

So at places like Manchester United, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Newcastle and Spurs there is anxiety about expectations not being met.

Xabi Alonso was hired to break the cycle at Chelsea and he is not yet succeeding

Xabi Alonso's side would appear to be the team that is failing without anybody seeming to notice.

At Stamford Bridge, the environment is conducive to Alonso and his team doing well this season.

Chelsea – not in Europe after last season's troubles – are only playing once a week. So Alonso – hired for his coaching reputation – has time on the grass with players who should arrive every weekend with freshness in their legs.

It's the environment that enabled Michael Carrick to fool everyone at Manchester United last season. While the rest of the Premier League got bogged down in the schedule, United sailed upwards on the back of a lighter load.

When we look at Alonso's team we see only familiar Chelsea things – and not in a good way.

Inconsistent tactics, some strange selections and, on the back of it, some very ordinary results.

This is the cycle Alonso was hired to break and he is not yet succeeding.

Sunday's defeat to Sunderland can be added to league setbacks against Spurs, Brentford and Arsenal.

They were unimpressive in beating United a couple of weeks ago also. Carrick's team outplayed them in the first half and should have been two or three goals ahead.

Under Alonso, Chelsea are yet to establish an identity or discernible patterns. It is hard to know yet what his best back four (or five) looks like. In the absence of the injured striker Joao Pedro, Alonso seems happier to play without one rather than use Danny Welbeck, signed for just this scenario in the summer.

The absence of Joao Pedro is significant while Alonso is also without his first choice goalkeeper Emi Martinez. These things matter.

But Chelsea have a huge squad of international players. Maybe it's too big. Whatever the case Alonso must get the best out of it soon.

Nobody seems to be talking about how very underwhelming the whole thing feels. But if it continues, they soon will be.

On Match of the Day on Sunday night, football's most vanilla pundit Dion Dublin was asked whether Michael Carrick has done enough to keep his job.

'I think so,' said Dublin. 'I think Michael has all the tools but the players just aren't doing what they need to do.'

At every other club in the Premier League, under-performing players and the bad results that tend to follow lead to intense scrutiny and criticism of the manager. It's his job to affect these things.

Not at United, though, where the level of public and media support for Carrick remains extraordinary and illogical.

If we applied this level of leeway to everybody else then nobody would ever be sacked.

Dion Dublin, pictured on Homes Under The Hammer duty, gave Michael Carrick an easy ride

Carrick is out of his depth at sinking Manchester United - his team are a shambles

Yes, there are a number of factors at play at Old Trafford. Yes, we know what they are and who is to blame for them. Yes, it's a very difficult job.

But the truth is that Carrick is failing in a quite spectacular fashion.

Of all the managers to have followed Sir Alex Ferguson over the last 13 and a half years, Erik ten Hag was the one who looked most out of his depth in terms of the chaotic nature of his team's football.

Carrick is now on the way to eclipsing that. His team are a shambles and that's on him. Once again, this is a mediocre league and it's quite criminal that Carrick has his group of players in the bottom three.

The former Middlesbrough manager is so out of his depth it's quite painful to watch.

It was another extraordinary afternoon at Old Trafford as United drew 4-4 with Aston Villa.

Unai Emery's Villa team is going through yet another regeneration after the sale of big-name players in the summer and balancing the Champions League with domestic football will once again be a challenge.

Emery seems to have made his mind up about one of his squad members, though, after former United and Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday.

Garnacho is a talented player but has made only 14 Premier League starts – and none at Villa – since leaving Old Trafford for Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

The Argentine is still only 22 so time is on his side but at some point he is going to have to do something on the field to justify the investment in a career that is currently going nowhere.

Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday by Aston Villa

Sky's excellent touchline reporter Patrick Davison had his work cut out post-match at Old Trafford as he interviewed one manager in danger of the sack and another who had just flounced down the tunnel like a chap with his pants on fire.

Neither Michael Carrick nor Unai Emery seemed particularly comfortable in the face of Davison's questions and that's exactly as it should be.

He is there to ask questions on behalf of a broadcaster that ploughs billions of pounds into our national sport each year. He is not there to apply soothing balm.

There would appear to be many others happy to do that anyway.

Sky's Patrick Davison (right) is not there to apply soothing balm with his questions

Less impressive was the appearance of Sky's latest metric that appeared on screen during Nottingham Forest's dismantling of Manchester City on Saturday.

Titled simply 'pressures' it indicated that Forest were doing rather better at it than City.

But what did it mean? Does anybody know? Or indeed care?

Two seasons ago at the City Ground I saw local boy Ryan Yates give Casemiro such a chasing as Forest beat Manchester United that the great Brazilian was taken off before he was sent off.

On Saturday by the river, Yates made his first league start of the season as Oliver Glasner’s team overwhelmed City.

Beforehand Yates gave an address to his team-mates. He told them about what it meant to play for the club and touched briefly on its history.

He told me once in an interview that he tends to tell all new arrivals at Forest what the two stars on the shirt actually mean – two European Cups won in 1979 and 1980.

It’s smart work by a lad who knows what football means in Nottingham and it was smart work by his manager who knew that his team needed an injection of something visceral to drag him from a trough of failure that was threatening to cost him his job.

Manchester United could probably do with a bit of that right now. So, possibly, could Chelsea and indeed Tottenham. At Liverpool, they lament the absence from the team of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones.

It takes an awful lot to make up a Premier League team these days. Place of birth is not a priority any more and that’s understandable. But sometimes it helps.

When was the last time an English team won the title with a poor goalkeeper?

Flick back over the last couple of decades and it's hard to find an example.

So what hope for Manchester City this season?

Gianluigi Donnarumma is anything but a poor goalkeeper but the problem is that he is playing like one and it is there that City's current problems start.

Enzo Maresca's back four looks shot to pieces and that often happens when they lose faith in the chap behind them.

Maresca says he won't change. 'My team is Gigi plus ten others,' is his take.

Enzo Maresca says he will not change goalkeeper despite Gianluigi Donnarumma's problems

His back up is 34-year-old Argentinean Geronimo Rulli, a member of his country's World Cup squad with nine caps to his name.

Rulli is well-travelled and has some pedigree. He was, for example, Villarreal's hero as they beat Manchester United in a Europa League final shoot out in 2021.

If Maresca trusts him then maybe now is the time to show it. If he doesn't then why did City sign him?

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is perhaps not quite what he once was at the age of 34 but produced a throwback performance for his team at Crystal Palace. Without him, Liverpool would not have won.

Nevertheless Palace's struggles go on and their coach Pierre Sage is in danger of losing his job.

However the south London club cannot say they were not warned about trouble ahead.

Former manager Oliver Glasner spent most of last season in a huff about what he saw as a failure by the Palace board to invest properly in the squad.

Palace have won twice in ten Premier League games this season and it seems Glasner may have been right.

Brighton continue to fly high and to produce such an energetic performance to beat Brentford having played away at Getafe in Europe on Thursday was testimony to the fitness of Fabian Hurzeler's squad.

The Seagulls were certainly helped by having to play against ten for an hour, though, and on Match of the Day the enduringly listenable Jonathan Pearce spoke for all of us as he watched Chema Andres go down after minimal contact to his cheek from Brentford's Igor Thiago.

'That was nothing, nothing, nothing,' said Pearce as Thiago walked off.

Coming so soon after theatrics from Alexis MacAllister and Gabriel in the Liverpool-Arsenal game last week, the issue of players exaggerating facial contact to get opponents sent off remains a live one.

Brentford's manager Keith Andrews was measured on the issue but suggested the tactic was becoming 'a game within a game'.

It's a problem and referees head Howard Webb needs his officials to get a grip of it.

Brighton's Pascal Gross has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates this season and that's more than anyone else in the Premier League.

Gross cost £1.2million when he returned to the club from Borussia Dortmund last January.

It constitutes another steal in the market by Brighton's stat boffins but this time they probably didn't need the data to convince them of its merits.

Pascal Gross scored on Sunday and has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates

Bournemouth, meanwhile, cast their net as widely as anybody these days and that includes all the way down the English pyramid.

The South Coast club – on an eight-match winning streak now under Marco Rose – have a relationship with yesterday's FA Cup giant killers Wimborne from the seventh tier.

Wimborne of the Southern League Premier South beat League Two Crawley in Round One and will this week send their Chilean teenage striker Angel Diaz for a trial at the Premier League club.

Story of last season in the EFL was probably Lincoln City's promotion to the Championship where, after 15 games, they are just about keeping their heads above water in 21st place.

Architect of that incredible rise was former futsal coach Michael Skubala who rather sullied the romantic feel of it all by quitting almost immediately to join Bristol City.

This weekend Skubala's team were thrashed 5-0 at home by Norwich with the home fans singing that their manager would be 'sacked in the morning'.

Lincoln have already won at Ashton Gate, back in September, at the start of a run that has seen City win just two from ten.

Sometimes, it really does pay just to stay where you are.

Substitute captain Federico Valverde struck in stoppage time as Real Madrid twice came from behind to beat AEK Athens 3-2. The win keeps Mourinho's side perfect in the league phase and takes them past his qualification target, days before a trip to Valencia without Vinícius.

Federico Valverde came off the bench in Athens and settled a match Real Madrid had trailed twice. The captain’s long-range strike arrived in the second minute of stoppage time. It completed another away comeback in this Champions League campaign. Mourinho’s side remain perfect after four matchdays.

AEK struck first. Koita put the hosts ahead in the 12th minute. Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside after a review just before the half-hour. He did not have to wait long. In the 32nd minute he equalised with a backheel from Cucurella’s cross.

AEK went ahead again with 15 minutes of normal time left. Stavros Pilios ran onto a pass from Koita and shot through Courtois’s legs. Madrid answered in less than three minutes. Denzel Dumfries played a low ball across goal and Mbappé made it 2-2.

The night ended badly for Koita. AEK’s opening scorer was sent off at 90+5, after the final whistle. He had kept protesting to the referee despite repeated warnings.

The winner carried extra weight given Valverde’s recent fitness. He felt strong discomfort in his right hamstring in the 23rd minute of the 2-1 Clásico win at Camp Nou. Mourinho said afterwards that Valverde had played more than 40 minutes injured. In Athens he started on the bench, yet still had the final say.

Madrid’s European record now reads four wins from four. They beat Inter 2-1 at home, came back to win 4-3 at Roma and beat Leipzig 4-1 at home before this trip. Their tally of 12 points takes them past the 11–12 point mark Mourinho set as the target for qualification. The next aim is a top-eight finish.

The pattern is notable. Both the Roma and AEK wins came after Madrid had fallen behind away from home. In Athens they had to respond on two separate occasions.

Attention now turns to LaLiga, where Madrid remain without Vinícius. On 16 October, the RFEF Appeals Committee rejected the club’s appeal and upheld his ban. Two games were for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair against Villarreal. The other two were for confronting the referee afterwards.

Lamine Yamal became the Champions League's top scorer before the age of 20 as Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0, taking the mark from Kylian Mbappé. The record comes soon after Mbappé's double decided the Clásico, and the win lifts Barça to second in the league phase.

Lamine Yamal has taken a Champions League scoring record from Kylian Mbappé. He opened the scoring in Barcelona’s win over Aston Villa at Spotify Camp Nou on 3 November. Yamal needed 37 Champions League appearances to reach his total. He does not turn 20 until next July. The record could therefore grow further this season. #1232. Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

The lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the issues Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

Thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

Thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N

The last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major issue for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a big day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

“We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

It might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

What they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

James Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU

The roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

Hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI

It must be said the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

The whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

He did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

#1229. Declan Rice reveals he's stepped back from social media because it can 'ruin your whole day' after sick trolling of him and his girlfriend - as he poses in new photoshoot

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:36 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 08:45 EST, 9 November 2026

Declan Rice has opened up about reducing his use of social media - citing the mental toll it can have.

The Arsenal and England midfielder has been subjected to online abuse in the past - with his long-term partner Lauren Fryer having also been targeted.

Online abuse about her appearance had led to Fryer wiping all posts from her Instagram page back in 2024.

While Rice still has an Instagram account, he quit X three years ago as a result of the negativity that app can bring.

'I've not been back on the app since,' he told GQ Magazine - after being named among their Men of the Year. 'You could be having a great morning. You read one thing, and it just ruins your whole day.

'I feel like that's one of my strongest points... the ability to block out noise and not deal with that kind of stuff.'

Declan Rice has revealed he quit X three years ago due to the abuse he would receive online

Rice and long-term partner Lauren Fryer have been targeted in the past (pair pictured with their son Jude in May)

The midfielder says one post could 'ruin' his whole day - even if he was a great day beforehand

Rice, who has a four-year-old son called Jude with Fryer, is worried about the impact of social media on the younger generations.

'Screen time, for me, isn't a big thing,' he says of his own personal phone usage. 'I think social media for kids is 100 per cent a problem. I don't feel like there's as much personality now as there was a few years ago.'

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport last month, the 27-year-old is closing in on a new long-term deal at Arsenal believed to be worth around £350,000 per week.

The contract will put him on a level footing with Bukayo Saka at the top of the club's salary list.

And speaking about money in football as a whole, Rice told GQ Magazine that the finances within the sport are 'ridiculous' and despite his wealth he still wants to set a good example to his son Jude.

'The money that's in football as a whole is just ridiculous,' he continued. 'It's important to understand what things cost, even if you don't have to worry about paying for them.

'You still want to teach your kid values, not wanting them to be spoiled. You want them to work and to understand the value of life and money.

'It makes you more comfortable to be able to do things. But I don't wake up and think, "Oh, I've got loads of money", it's not the end goal.'

The 27-year-old is worried about the pitfalls of social media on the younger generations

The 27-year-old Arsenal and England star has been named in GQ Magazine's Men of the Year

Rice's focus will now be on his country with England hosting Croatia on Thursday night in the UEFA Nations League before travelling to World Cup champions Spain on Sunday.

Going into the November international break, the midfielder is enjoying a fine season with Arsenal who sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League with 27 points from their opening 10 matches.

#1227. Güler scores and assists as Real Madrid win at Mestalla to draw level with Barcelona

Arda Güler scored once and set up another as José Mourinho's Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to reach 30 points, level with Barcelona, before the international break. Valencia are second from bottom in their last season at Mestalla.

Federico Valverde put Madrid ahead at Mestalla in the 28th minute on Saturday 7 November 2026. Güler doubled the lead eight minutes later. Jude Bellingham reached the byline and pulled the ball back. Güler met it first time and finished with his right foot.

Güler could have had more. Stole Dimitrievski stopped him twice: a strong shot from the edge of the area in the 43rd minute and a one-on-one in the 54th.

Kylian Mbappé’s strike in the 75th minute made it three. That goal stretched his scoring run to seven matches in a row. He has 12 league goals, three behind Barcelona’s Raphinha at the top of the scoring chart.

The visitors had 68% of the ball and completed 568 passes to Valencia’s 225. They took 19 shots, 11 of them on target. Valencia managed four shots and just two on target. Expected goals finished 2.39 to 0.26 in Madrid’s favour.

The hosts’ best moment came around the 20th minute. Aaron Mayol won the ball just outside the area and forced Thibaut Courtois to stretch for a save. Aguirre sent on Luis Rioja for Justin de Haas at half-time, but the pattern did not change.

Two wins from 12 league games is all Valencia have to show so far. Only Malaga, on 5 points, are below them. Aguirre has one win from his five league games in charge. The club is already promoting season-ticket prices for the new Nou Mestalla.

#1225. Premier League x Stonewall partnership ends, new LGBTQ+ campaign to be launched

The Premier League is set to introduce a new LGBTQ+ inclusion campaign after ending its partnership with Stonewall, the charity behind the widely recognised Rainbow Laces initiative.

Stonewallâs Rainbow Laces campaign, launched in 2013, became a fixture across English football, with players from all Premier League clubs wearing rainbow-coloured laces and captains donning rainbow armbands to promote acceptance and equality. The campaign aimed to support LGBTQ+ rights and foster inclusivity among fans and young people.

After over a decade of collaboration, the league will now lead its own campaign, timed to coincide with LGBTQ+ History Month in February, The Telegraph report.

"Rainbow Laces has benefited from a wide range of partners with a natural ebb and flow reflecting cultural and sporting changes," a Stonewall spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"Alongside other sporting bodies the FA has been instrumental in advancing LGBTQ+ inclusion at the grassroots level and more recently the Women's Super League has taken up the mantle as the women's game has grown - enabling Rainbow Laces to reach more diverse audiences."

Despite Stonewall's efforts, recent reports from Kick It Out reveal an alarming increase in discriminatory incidents in football, including rises in sexism, transphobia and faith-based abuse, with racism continuing to be the most prevalent issue.

Controversies around playersâ attitudes to rainbow armbands have also made headlines. Last season, Ipswich captain Sam Morsy declined to wear one due to religious beliefs, while Crystal Palaceâs Marc GuÃ©hi faced criticism for personalising his armband with the phrase âI Love Jesus.â

Additionally, Manchester United scrapped plans for LGBTQ+ support jackets after a player refused to participate.

With no openly gay or bisexual players currently in the Premier League, and the surge in discriminatory incidents, some question the timing of the split from Stonewall â an organisation highly respected for its work in LGBTQ+ advocacy.

Details of the Premier Leagueâs new campaign are still under wraps, but as the league presses âreset,â thereâs hope it will introduce a meaningful and effective initiative that advances equality rather than undermines it.

#1223. Late Buchanan and Carlos Romero goals give Villarreal 2-0 win over Getafe

Villarreal ended a two-game losing run on Sunday, 8 November, with a home win over Getafe in matchday 12 of LaLiga. Both goals came in the final 10 minutes at the Estadio de la Cerámica. Tajon Buchanan scored first and Carlos Romero added the second in stoppage time.

Iñigo Pérez’s side came into the game after a 0-1 league defeat to Espanyol and a 0-6 loss to Paris Saint-Germain. They controlled almost all of the afternoon, with 73% of the ball and 566 passes to Getafe’s 220.

The first half finished goalless. Getafe goalkeeper David Soria made 5 saves and was rated 7.27, the best mark among Pepe Bordalás’s players. Villarreal finished with 22 shots to 9. They had 7 on target, and Getafe managed just 1. Their expected goals figure of 2.38, against 0.68 for the visitors, reflected how one-sided the attacking play was.

Getafe picked up the first two bookings. Mario Martín was cautioned in the 32nd minute and Nemanja Gudelj in the 62nd, both for fouls. Getafe committed 13 fouls in total, and Villarreal committed 6. Santi Comesaña and Renato Veiga were then booked for the home side in the 67th and 76th minutes.

The breakthrough came in the 80th minute. Nicolas Pépé set up Buchanan, who had 4 shots across the afternoon. In the first minute of stoppage time, Ayoze Pérez supplied the assist for Carlos Romero to make the game safe. Ayoze created 3 chances in his 27 minutes on the pitch.

Carlos Romero capped his 90 minutes with the goal and was rated 7.84, the highest of any player. Logan Costa was close behind on 7.8, and Buchanan received 7.69.

The result repeats Villarreal’s win by the same scoreline over Getafe at La Cerámica on 6 December 2025. Getafe had won the most recent meeting 2-1 at home in February. Across the last six league encounters between the clubs, Villarreal now have three wins, Getafe one, and two have been drawn.

Villarreal are eighth with 15 points from 12 games, three behind sixth-placed Sevilla. Getafe are 15th on 12 points with a goal difference of -10. They have now lost two in a row in all competitions, after a 0-1 defeat to Brighton preceded this trip.

Both sides face difficult fixtures on Sunday 22 November. Villarreal travel to leaders Barcelona, who have 33 points. Getafe host third-placed Atlético Madrid.

#1222. Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick

So where do Manchester United go from here? It is never a good look when opposition fans start willing a rival club to stick with their manager, but that was the ignominy that had befallen Michael Carrick by the end of an afternoon in which Lisandro Martinez’s latest plastic hardman impression embodied the very worst of United’s self-sabotage.

After seeing their team go 2-0 up when Cole Palmer converted the penalty given away by Martinez’s lunacy, the Chelsea fans taunted Carrick with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” and later “You’re going down with the City”, a nod to the other Manchester club who are crisis torn for very different reasons.

As the final whistle loomed, though, and with United just grateful Estevao had not punished Martinez’s red card more severely, the Chelsea fans had changed their tune. “Michael Carrick, we want you to stay,” came the chant from the Matthew Harding Stand and that cut far deeper.

And to think that the opening 45 minutes had offered United and their fans some hope of a little respite from the storm before ultimately giving way to an ever-darkening gloom.

Carrick, who had been given a stay of execution in midweek, said he still expected to be in charge for Roma’s visit to Old Trafford on Tuesday in the Champions League. But it is hard to escape the feeling that another managerial change will be coming at United before too long even if no one can be sure what happens next.

Equally, the prospect of more upheaval in the dugout might elicit little more than a shrug from fans pointing the finger squarely at the ownership and the executives they have appointed. The players were spared this time but Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers remained the target of sustained abuse as did Jason Wilcox, the director of football.

Defeat here extended United’s winless run to nine matches, their worst sequence for 38 years. They have taken just four points from the last 21 on offer in the Premier League and seem to be sinking fast. Carrick was asked about the team becoming mired in a relegation battle. This is the territory United are in.

The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

The Old Trafford hierarchy gave Carrick a stay of execution in midweek and, when asked if he expected to still to be at the helm when United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, the head coach replied: “Yes. I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.”

“Why are they not in the top six?” asked Ferguson. “To me they’re cheating their manager. As for Chelsea, who were awful in defeat by Brentford and Spurs either side of impressive victories over Bournemouth and at Everton, they need to find some defensive solidity, discipline and a way of terrorising defences in the absence of Joao Pedro. #1216. Inside the world of Captain Chaos at Man United: Michael Carrick will not walk away but here's what the players are saying as they fail to respond to his direction, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 08:52 EST, 9 November 2026

While the Manchester United fans who had gone ahead with a booze boycott of Old Trafford watched in horror as their team teetered on the brink of total collapse and head coach Michael Carrick clung to his job, you couldn't help but think of Lloyd Bridges as Steve McCroskey, the frazzled air traffic control boss in Airplane! 'Looks like I picked the wrong week to quit drinking!'

God knows United have forced their supporters to hit the bottle this season, not least in the past six days when they have handed a two-goal advantage to Roma and Aston Villa (twice) and still managed to salvage a win and a draw.

But this cannot carry on. As cavalier as United like to be, this is not the way to play football.

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, it's great for the Sky Sports cameras beaming it live and the Amazon Prime documentary makers filming behind the scenes, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch.

Nowhere in the UEFA coaching manuals will you find a chapter on routinely conceding the first two goals being a sensible route to success. For all his bluster after a bonkers 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Carrick knows it and his players know it.

'After we concede goals we show character, but if we do this before we can win much more games,' said Matheus Cunha. 'I don't know why, everyone tries to get answers for that. We want to be the best and show that we can come back. We need to show the mentality to do this from the start.'

As Manchester United head coach, Michael Carrick is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos

Coming out swinging every game like a boxer on his last legs is great for entertainment, but it is not evidence of solid preparation on the training pitch

It isn't just in the last week either. United were a goal down against Atletico Madrid inside the first minute and Como in the second. They were two down to Villa after three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest that has happened to United in the Premier League era.

This is not a coincidence. It is not bad luck. This is in the mind-set of these Manchester United players, and the game management of Carrick – and that is what should worry Old Trafford bosses the most.

As if being in the relegation zone for the next two weeks after a start of one win from 10 games – the worst since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago – is not bad enough, United don't seem to be playing to a plan. They are not responding to direction. They are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails.

Carrick made reference to it when he spoke before this game, admitting that the players are better when they don't think too much.

'Momentum within games, day-to-day, week-to-week, game-to-game, it's huge,' he said at Carrington on Friday. 'I think it's important with your feelings and your emotions to roll with it. Then your memory can click in and you realise, 'Oh yeah, this is what it feels like, this is how it should be', and you start seeing different things.

'It's all got to come together, but feeling, confidence, and that emotion and sometimes not even thinking. You're at your best when you don't think too much and you just trust and play on instinct, and I think we did a lot of that the other night (against Roma).'

The irony is that Carrick was so measured, so composed as a player. Now, as coach, he is doing a convincing impersonation of Captain Chaos. United's games are reminiscent of the high-scoring madness of Erik ten Hag's last full season in charge, devoid of stability or structure.

That is what Carrick's employers need to consider when they sit down to discuss whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge which guided the club towards third place and Champions League qualification.

Now they are third from bottom and will stay in the relegation zone for the duration of the international break. For three minutes on Sunday, Manchester United – the aristocrats of English football – were actually in last place after Sunderland took the lead against Chelsea and Crystal Palace were still goalless with Liverpool.

United don't seem to be playing to a plan or responding to direction - they are reverting to instinct and moments of skill when everything else fails

Carrick's employers need to consider  whether he can restore the sanity of his first four months in charge

That being in 18th place – one below Coventry – is somehow seen as blessed relief from the unrelenting humiliation of this season, says everything about the state of the club.

At the end of a week that marked 40 years since Ferguson's arrival and was celebrated by a dinner with many of his most famous players, it has been quite the fall from grace.

Which brings us back to the fans. They are a loyal bunch and once again serenaded Carrick off the pitch at full-time having spent much of the previous two hours slaughtering the owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Protest groups had urged them to boycott buying alcohol at the stadium to hit the Glazer family and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in the pocket. 'Your funeral not ours – sell up now,' read one new banner. 'We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners,' said another.

But they know their football at United. Was it support or just sympathy with a head coach who has done his best in an impossible situation?

Carrick says he won't walk away and they never do. On Remembrance Sunday, he stood there on the touchline with a poppy on his arm and hope in his heart that United could get themselves out of another self-inflicted crisis.

They did. Again. But how much longer can United and Carrick keep winging it, and believe that calm will emerge from the chaos.

His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

Maresca picked a midfield that cost £327m to recruit this summer, with Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi picked together for the first time. There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

The goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

“Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

It was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

“I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more important, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”
